title.zh: 卷四十九 列傳第十九 阮籍 嵇康 向秀 劉伶 謝鯤 胡毋輔之 畢卓 王尼 羊曼 光逸
title.en: Volume 49 Biographies 19: Ruan Ji; Ji Kang; Xiang Xiu; Liu Ling; Xie Kun; Huwu Fuzhi; Bi Zhuo; Wang Ni; Yang Man; Guang Yi
title.raw: 卷四十九 列傳第十九 阮籍 嵇康 向秀 劉伶 謝鯤 胡毋輔之 畢卓 王尼 羊曼 光逸 Volume 49 Biographies 19: Ruan Ji; Ji Kang; Xiang Xiu; Liu Ling; Xie Kun; Huwu Fuzhi; Bi Zhuo; Wang Ni; Yang Man; Guang Yi

sentences.zh: 阮籍，字嗣宗，陳留尉氏人也。

translations.literal: Ruan Ji, whose courtesy name was Sizong, was a native of Weishi in Chenliu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Ruan Ji, courtesy name Sizong, came from Weishi in Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 父瑀，魏丞相掾，知名於世。

translations.literal: His father Ruan Yu was a clerk on the staff of the Wei dynasty's Chancellor of State and was renowned in the world of his day.
translations.idiomatic: His father, Ruan Yu, served as a clerk to the Wei Chancellor and was widely known.

sentences.zh: 籍容貌瑰傑，志氣宏放，傲然獨得，任性不羈，而喜怒不形於色。

translations.literal: In appearance Ruan Ji was striking and magnificent; in aspiration and temper he was broad and unrestrained. Proud and self-contained, he followed his nature without restraint, yet joy and anger did not show in his face.
translations.idiomatic: He had a striking presence and a bold, expansive spirit—proud, self-possessed, and untrammeled—while his face betrayed neither joy nor anger.

sentences.zh: 或閉戶視書，累月不出；

translations.literal: Sometimes he shut his door and read books, not going out for months on end.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes he would shut himself in and read for months without stepping outside.

sentences.zh: 或登臨山水，經日忘歸。

translations.literal: Sometimes he climbed heights and wandered rivers and mountains, forgetting to return for whole days.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes he climbed hills and roamed streams until whole days passed and he forgot to go home.

sentences.zh: 博覽群籍，尤好《莊》《老》。

translations.literal: He read widely across the classics, especially loving Zhuangzi and Laozi.
translations.idiomatic: He read voraciously, with a particular love for the Zhuangzi and the Laozi.

sentences.zh: 嗜酒能嘯，善彈琴。

translations.literal: He was fond of wine, could whistle, and was skilled at playing the zither.
translations.idiomatic: He loved wine, could whistle, and played the zither with real skill.

sentences.zh: 當其得意，忽忘形骸。

translations.literal: When he was carried away by delight, he would suddenly forget body and limbs.
translations.idiomatic: In moments of elation he would quite forget his own body.

sentences.zh: 時人多謂之癡，惟族兄文業每嘆服之，以為勝己，由是咸共稱異。

translations.literal: People of the time mostly called him mad; only his elder clansman Ruan Wenye repeatedly sighed in admiration, believing him better than himself, whereupon all together praised him as extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Most contemporaries dismissed him as eccentric, but his kinsman Ruan Wenye often marveled and admitted Ruan Ji surpassed him—after which everyone spoke of him as remarkable.

sentences.zh: 籍嘗隨叔父至東郡，兗州刺史王昶請與相見，終日不開一言，自以不能測。

translations.literal: Once Ruan Ji accompanied an uncle to Dong commandery; the Inspector of Yanzhou, Wang Chang, asked to meet him, and they spent an entire day together, yet Ruan Ji never uttered a single word, so that Chang believed himself unable to plumb him.
translations.idiomatic: When he once traveled with an uncle to Dong commandery, Yanzhou Inspector Wang Chang requested an audience and sat with him all day, but Ruan Ji never spoke; Wang Chang concluded he could not be fathomed.

sentences.zh: 太尉蔣濟聞其有雋才而辟之，籍詣都亭奏記曰：「伏惟明公以含一之德，據上臺之位，英豪翹首，俊賢抗足。

translations.literal: The Grand Commandant Jiang Ji heard that he possessed outstanding talent and summoned him. Ruan Ji went to the courier lodge and submitted a memorial saying: "I humbly reflect that Your Excellency, with virtue embracing the One, occupies the highest seat; heroes crane their necks, worthy men stand on tiptoe.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commandant Jiang Ji, hearing of his talent, summoned him. Ruan Ji presented a memorial at the relay lodge: "You hold the summit of power with all-embracing virtue; heroes and talents strain to join you.

sentences.zh: 開府之日，人人自以為掾屬；

translations.literal: On the day the bureau opened, each man thought he would become your clerk;
translations.idiomatic: When you first opened your office, every man hoped to be named to your staff;

sentences.zh: 辟書始下，而下走為首。

translations.literal: when the summons was first issued, this humble person was placed first.
translations.idiomatic: when the appointment list appeared, my lowly name headed it.

sentences.zh: 昔子夏在於西河之上，而文侯擁篲；

translations.literal: In old days Zixia stood by the western river, and Marquis Wen of Wei attended him with broom in hand;
translations.idiomatic: Long ago Zixia taught west of the River, and Marquis Wen of Wei swept the path before him;

sentences.zh: 鄒子處於黍谷之陰，而昭王陪乘。

translations.literal: Zou Yan dwelled in the shade north of Millet Valley, and King Zhao of Yan rode beside him as chariot companion.
translations.idiomatic: Zou Yan lived north of Millet Valley, and King Zhao of Yan took the place beside him in the carriage.

sentences.zh: 夫布衣韋帶之士，孤居特立，王公大人所以禮下之者，為道存也。

translations.literal: As for common scholars in plain cloth who live apart and stand alone, the reason great lords and nobles lower themselves to them is that the Way is present in them.
translations.idiomatic: Poor scholars who stand apart are honored by lords because the Way still dwells in them.

sentences.zh: 今籍無鄒、卜之道，而有其陋，猥見采擇，無以稱當。

translations.literal: Now I lack the way of Zou or Bu Zixia, yet I share their lowliness; I have been rashly selected and have no means to answer fittingly.
translations.idiomatic: I have none of the learning of Zou Yan or Bu Zixia, only their obscurity; I was chosen by mistake and cannot live up to the role.

sentences.zh: 方將耕於東皋之陽，輸黍稷之餘稅。

translations.literal: I am about to plow on the sunny slope east of the marsh and pay in the surplus tax of millet and panicled millet.
translations.idiomatic: I mean to farm the sunny fields east of the marsh and pay my grain tax from the surplus.

sentences.zh: 負薪疲病，足力不強，補吏之召，非所克堪。

translations.literal: Bearing firewood I am worn and ill; my legs are not strong; a clerk's summons is not something I can bear.
translations.idiomatic: I am worn thin hauling fuel and my legs are weak; I cannot sustain the duties of a clerk.

sentences.zh: 乞回謬恩，以光清舉。

translations.literal: I beg you to withdraw this misplaced favor and thereby brighten a proper selection."
translations.idiomatic: Please withdraw this undeserved kindness and keep your recommendation unsullied."

sentences.zh: 」初，濟恐籍不至，得記欣然。

translations.literal: " At first Jiang Ji had feared Ruan Ji would not come; when he received the memorial he was delighted.
translations.idiomatic: At first Jiang Ji had worried Ruan Ji might refuse; the memorial delighted him.

sentences.zh: 遣卒迎之，而籍已去，濟大怒。

translations.literal: He sent soldiers to welcome him, but Ruan Ji had already departed, and Ji was greatly angered.
translations.idiomatic: He sent men to escort him in, only to find Ruan Ji had already left; Jiang Ji was furious.

sentences.zh: 於是鄉親共喻之，乃就吏。

translations.literal: Thereupon his fellow villagers together explained matters to him, and he then took office.
translations.idiomatic: Villagers and kin together reasoned with him, and he finally accepted the appointment.

sentences.zh: 後謝病歸。

translations.literal: Later he resigned citing illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he pleaded illness and went home.

sentences.zh: 復為尚書郎，少時，又以病免。

translations.literal: He again served as Gentleman of the Masters of Writing; after a short time again was dismissed on account of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Gentleman of the Masters of Writing but, within a short while, again left office citing illness.

sentences.zh: 及曹爽輔政，召為參軍。

translations.literal: When Cao Shuang assisted the government he summoned him as an adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Shuang directed the government, he summoned Ruan Ji as an adjutant.

sentences.zh: 籍因以疾辭，屏於田里。

translations.literal: Ruan Ji therefore declined on grounds of illness and withdrew among the fields and villages.
translations.idiomatic: Ruan Ji pleaded illness and withdrew to the countryside.

sentences.zh: 歲余而爽誅，時人服其遠識。

translations.literal: After more than a year Shuang was executed; people of the time admired his foresight.
translations.idiomatic: A little over a year later Cao Shuang was executed; contemporaries admired his foresight.

sentences.zh: 宣帝為太傅，命籍為從事中郎。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan (Sima Yi) was Grand Tutor he appointed Ruan Ji gentleman of the staff for miscellaneous purposes.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan held the Grand Tutorship, he named Ruan Ji a miscellaneous aide.

sentences.zh: 及帝崩，復為景帝大司馬從事中郎。

translations.literal: When the emperor died he again served Emperor Jing (Sima Shi) as gentleman of the staff to the Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: After that ruler's death he again served Emperor Jing as aide to the Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 高貴鄉公即位，封關內侯，徙散騎常侍。

translations.literal: When the Duke of Gaoling District came to the throne he was enfeoffed as marquis within the passes and transferred to Regular Cavalier Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When the Duke of Gaoling ascended the throne, Ruan Ji was enfeoffed as a marquis within the passes and promoted to Regular Cavalier Attendant.

sentences.zh: 籍本有濟世志，屬魏、晉之際，天下多故，名士少有全者，籍由是不與世事，遂酣飲為常。

translations.literal: Ruan Ji originally harbored a mind to save the age; but with the transition between Wei and Jin and constant troubles in the realm, few famous scholars survived whole, so Ruan Ji ceased involvement in public affairs and took constant drunkenness as his norm.
translations.idiomatic: He had once hoped to aid the world, but as Wei gave way to Jin and turmoil mounted, few eminent men escaped with their lives, so he turned away from affairs and sought refuge in perpetual drinking.

sentences.zh: 文帝初欲為武帝求婚於籍，籍醉六十日，不得言而止。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen (Sima Zhao) first wished to seek a marriage alliance for Emperor Wu (Sima Yan) with Ruan Ji, Ruan Ji stayed drunk for sixty days, so that nothing could be said and the matter stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Zhao first tried to arrange a marriage between his son Sima Yan and Ruan Ji's family, Ruan Ji drank himself insensible for sixty days until the matchmakers could get nowhere and the plan died.

sentences.zh: 鐘會數以時事問之，欲因其可否而致之罪，皆以酣醉獲免。

translations.literal: Zhong Hui several times questioned him on current affairs, intending to use his assent or denial to bring a charge against him; each time he escaped by deep drunkenness.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Hui repeatedly pressed him on state affairs, hoping to trap him in a damaging answer; each time Ruan Ji drank his way out of danger.

sentences.zh: 及文帝輔政，籍嘗從容言於帝曰：「籍平生曾游東平，樂其風土。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen took charge of government, Ruan Ji once spoke at his ease to the emperor, saying, "In life I once wandered to Dongping and enjoyed its customs and land.
translations.idiomatic: Once Sima Zhao was regent, Ruan Ji remarked casually, "I have visited Dongping and love its people and landscape.

sentences.zh: 」帝大悅，即拜東平相。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and at once appointed him governor of Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: Delighted, the regent immediately named him governor of Dongping.

sentences.zh: 籍乘驢到郡，壞府舍屏鄣，使內外相望，法令清簡，旬日而還。

translations.literal: Ruan Ji rode a donkey to the commandery, tore down the screens and partitions of the yamen so that inside and outside looked on one another, kept laws and orders clear and simple, and returned within ten days.
translations.idiomatic: He arrived on a donkey, stripped the office of its screens so clerks and public faced one another, simplified the statutes, and resigned within ten days.

sentences.zh: 帝引為大將軍從事中郎。

translations.literal: The emperor appointed him gentleman of the staff to the General-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was then recalled as aide to the General-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 有司言有子殺母者，籍曰：「嘻！

translations.literal: A responsible official reported that there was someone who had killed his mother; Ruan Ji said, "Ah!
translations.idiomatic: When officials reported a case of a son who had killed his mother, Ruan Ji exclaimed, "Well!

sentences.zh: 殺父乃可，至殺母乎！

translations.literal: Killing the father might be allowed—how could it extend to killing the mother!"
translations.idiomatic: Killing one's father might be imaginable—but killing one's mother?"

sentences.zh: 」坐者怪其失言。

translations.literal: Those seated thought his words strange and erroneous.
translations.idiomatic: The assembly thought he had spoken monstrously.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「殺父，天下之極惡，而以為可乎？

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Killing the father is the worst evil in the world—do you think it acceptable?"
translations.idiomatic: The regent asked, "Matricide aside, do you call patricide acceptable?"

sentences.zh: 」籍曰：「禽獸知母而不知父，殺父，禽獸之類也。

translations.literal: Ruan Ji said, "Birds and beasts know the mother and do not know the father. To kill the father belongs to the class of birds and beasts.
translations.idiomatic: Ruan Ji replied, "Beasts know their dams, not their sires; to slay a father is still the act of a beast.

sentences.zh: 殺母，禽獸之不若。

translations.literal: To kill the mother is not to be as birds and beasts."
translations.idiomatic: To slay a mother sinks below even beasts."

sentences.zh: 」眾乃悅服。

translations.literal: Then the crowd was appeased and convinced.
translations.idiomatic: The listeners were satisfied.

sentences.zh: 籍聞步兵廚營人善釀，有貯酒三百斛，乃求為步兵校尉。

translations.literal: Hearing that the men of the infantry kitchen camp brewed good wine and had three hundred hu stored, he asked to be colonel of the infantry garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that the infantry commissary kept excellent wine—three hundred hu in store—he requested appointment as colonel of the infantry garrison.

sentences.zh: 遺落世事，雖去佐職，恆遊府內，朝宴必與焉。

translations.literal: He neglected worldly affairs; although he had left the adjutant's post, he constantly roamed within the headquarters and invariably attended court feasts.
translations.idiomatic: He let worldly duties slide; though no longer adjutant, he still haunted headquarters and never missed the regent's banquets.

sentences.zh: 會帝讓九錫，公卿將勸進，使籍為其辭。

translations.literal: When the emperor declined the Nine Bestowals, the dukes and ministers were about to urge him onward and had Ruan Ji draft the text.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Zhao declined the Nine Bestowals, high ministers prepared a joint memorial of urging and charged Ruan Ji with the draft.

sentences.zh: 籍沈醉忘作，臨詣府，使取之，見籍方據案醉眠。

translations.literal: Ruan Ji was sunk in drink and forgot to compose it; when the deadline came they sent someone to fetch it, and found Ruan Ji sprawled drunk, asleep at his desk.
translations.idiomatic: He was too drunk to write; when the courier arrived at the office, Ruan Ji was slumped over his desk in a stupor.

sentences.zh: 使者以告，籍便書案，使寫之，無所改竄。

translations.literal: The messenger reported; Ruan Ji then wrote on the case and had him copy it out, without altering a word.
translations.idiomatic: Told the deadline had come, he scribbled the text on the document case and had the envoy copy it off unchanged.

sentences.zh: 辭甚清壯，為時所重。

translations.literal: The language was exceedingly clear and forceful and was esteemed in his time.
translations.idiomatic: The prose was lucid and powerful and won wide admiration.

sentences.zh: 籍雖不拘禮教，然發言玄遠，口不臧否人物。

translations.literal: Although he did not bind himself by ritual teaching, his utterances were abstruse and far-reaching, and he did not praise or blame particular persons in conversation.
translations.idiomatic: He flouted conventional ritual, yet his words ran deep and remote, and he refused to pass judgment on people in ordinary talk.

sentences.zh: 性至孝，母終，正與人圍棋，對者求止，籍留與決賭。

translations.literal: He was utterly filial: when his mother died he was in the middle of a weiqi game; his opponent asked to stop, but Ruan Ji kept him to finish the wager.
translations.idiomatic: He was profoundly filial, yet when news came that his mother had died he insisted on finishing a weiqi game though his opponent begged to stop.

sentences.zh: 既而飲酒二斗，舉聲一號，吐血數升。

translations.literal: Then he drank two dou of wine, gave one great cry, and vomited several sheng of blood.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did he drain two dou of wine, utter a single wrenching cry, and bring up several sheng of blood.

sentences.zh: 及將葬，食一蒸肫，飲二斗酒，然後臨訣，直言窮矣，舉聲一號，因又吐血數升，毀瘠骨立，殆致滅性。

translations.literal: When it came time for the burial he ate one steamed pig's trotter, drank two dou of wine, then went to take leave; he said plainly he was utterly spent, gave one great cry, and again vomited several sheng of blood; he wasted away until only bones stood, nearly destroying his nature.
translations.idiomatic: At the funeral he ate a steamed pig's trotter, drank two dou more, bade the coffin farewell saying he was utterly spent, cried out again, and vomited more blood; he wasted to skin and bone, nearly following his mother in death.

sentences.zh: 裴楷往弔之，籍散發箕踞，醉而直視，楷弔唁畢便去。

translations.literal: When Pei Kai came to condole, Ruan Ji let his hair fall loose and sat with legs sprawled, drunk and staring straight ahead; when Kai finished his condolences he left.
translations.idiomatic: When Pei Kai came to mourn, Ruan Ji sat hair unbound, legs sprawled, drunk and staring blankly; Pei Kai completed the rites and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 或問楷：「凡弔者，主哭，客乃為禮。

translations.literal: Someone asked Kai, "Ordinarily the host weeps and the guest then observes the rites.
translations.idiomatic: Someone asked Pei Kai, "At a wake the host leads the weeping before the guest pays respect.

sentences.zh: 籍既不哭，君何為哭？

translations.literal: Since Ruan Ji does not weep, why do you weep?"
translations.idiomatic: Ruan Ji never wept—why did you?"

sentences.zh: 」楷曰：「阮籍既方外之士，故不崇禮典。

translations.literal: Kai said, "Ruan Ji is already a man beyond this world, therefore he does not honor the ritual canon.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Kai answered, "Ruan Ji stands outside the world of convention, so ritual does not bind him.

sentences.zh: 我俗中之士，故以軌儀自居。

translations.literal: I am a man within the world, therefore I keep to formal observance myself."
translations.idiomatic: I remain inside it, so I observe the forms myself."

sentences.zh: 」時人歎為兩得。

translations.literal: People of the time sighed that both had done right.
translations.idiomatic: Onlookers said both men had acted fittingly.

sentences.zh: 籍又能為青白眼，見禮俗之士，以白眼對之。

translations.literal: Ruan Ji could also show the "blue eye" and the "white eye": when he met men of vulgar ritual he confronted them with the white eye.
translations.idiomatic: He could greet people with a "white eye" or a "blue eye": pedants of the ritualists' stamp received only the white.

sentences.zh: 及嵇喜來弔，籍作白眼，喜不懌而退。

translations.literal: When Ji Xi came to condole he gave the white eye; Xi was displeased and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When Ji Xi came to offer condolences, Ruan Ji showed him the white eye; Ji Xi left in annoyance.

sentences.zh: 喜弟康聞之，乃齎酒挾琴造焉，籍大悅，乃見青眼。

translations.literal: Xi's younger brother Ji Kang heard of it, then brought wine tucked under his arm and the zither and paid a visit; Ruan Ji was greatly pleased and showed the blue eye.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Xi's brother Ji Kang arrived bearing wine and a zither; Ruan Ji brightened and turned on him the blue eye of welcome.

sentences.zh: 由是禮法之士疾之若仇，而帝每保護之。

translations.literal: Thereupon men of ritual and law hated him like an enemy, yet the emperor always protected him.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual moralists loathed him, yet the regent shielded him.

sentences.zh: 籍嫂嘗歸甯，籍相見與別。

translations.literal: Ruan Ji's sister-in-law once went home to her parents' house, and Ruan Ji met and bade her farewell.
translations.idiomatic: When his sister-in-law returned to her natal family, Ruan Ji saw her off in person.

sentences.zh: 或譏之，籍曰：「禮豈為我設邪！

translations.literal: Some ridiculed him; Ruan Ji said, "Was ritual made for people like me?"
translations.idiomatic: Critics scoffed; he retorted, "Were the rites written for the likes of me?"

sentences.zh: 」鄰家少婦有美色，當壚沽酒。

translations.literal: A neighbor's young wife had beauty and tended the wine-shop counter.
translations.idiomatic: A neighbor's pretty young wife kept the wine shop.

sentences.zh: 籍嘗詣飲，醉，便臥其側。

translations.literal: Ruan Ji often went there to drink, got drunk, and lay down at her side.
translations.idiomatic: Ruan Ji would drink there until drunk and sleep beside her counter.

sentences.zh: 籍既不自嫌，其夫察之，亦不疑也。

translations.literal: Ruan Ji did not scruple on his account; her husband watched him and never suspected him.
translations.idiomatic: He saw nothing improper in it, and her husband, watching closely, never distrusted him.

sentences.zh: 兵家女有才色，未嫁而死。

translations.literal: There was a soldier's daughter with talent and beauty who died before she married.
translations.idiomatic: A soldier's talented, beautiful daughter died unwed.

sentences.zh: 籍不識其父兄，徑往哭之，盡哀而還。

translations.literal: Ruan Ji did not know her father or elder brothers but went straight to weep for her, exhausted his grief, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Ruan Ji, a stranger to her family, walked straight in to weep out his grief and left.

sentences.zh: 其外坦蕩而內淳至，皆此類也。

translations.literal: Outwardly he was expansive, inwardly utterly true: his conduct was all of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: Open and easy outwardly, inwardly he was utterly sincere—such was his way in everything.

sentences.zh: 時率意獨駕，不由徑路，車跡所窮，輒慟哭而反。

translations.literal: Often he drove carelessly alone, not following tracks or paths; wherever the ruts of the carriage ended he would wail loudly and turn back.
translations.idiomatic: He would drive alone wherever whim took him; when the road ended he would burst into tears and turn back.

sentences.zh: 嘗登廣武，觀楚、漢戰處，歎曰：「時無英雄，使豎子成名！

translations.literal: He once ascended Guangwu and viewed the place where Chu and Han fought, sighing, "In that age there were no heroes, so petty fellows won the fame!"
translations.idiomatic: Climbing Guangwu Pass to the old Chu–Han battlefield, he sighed, "No true heroes in that hour—so mediocrities won the renown!"

sentences.zh: 」登武牢山，望京邑而歎，於是賦《豪傑詩》。

translations.literal: He climbed Mount Wulao, gazed toward the capital, and sighed; thereupon he composed "Poem on Heroes."
translations.idiomatic: From Mount Wulao he looked toward Luoyang and sighed, then composed his "Poem on Heroes."

sentences.zh: 景元四年冬卒，時年五十四。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of the Jingyuan reign period, in winter, he died, aged fifty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the winter of Wei Jingyuan 4 (263 CE) at the age of fifty-four.

sentences.zh: 籍能屬文，初不留思。

translations.literal: Ruan Ji could compose prose without advance deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: He could write at speed without brooding beforehand.

sentences.zh: 作《詠懷詩》八十餘篇，為世所重。

translations.literal: He wrote more than eighty pieces of "Poems of Lament from the Heart," valued by the world.
translations.idiomatic: His eighty-odd "Poems Singing My Cares" became classics of the age.

sentences.zh: 著《達莊論》，敘無為之貴。

translations.literal: He composed "On Comprehending Zhuangzi," setting forth the value of non-action.
translations.idiomatic: His essay "Mastering the Zhuangzi" praised the worth of non-action.

sentences.zh: 文多不錄。

translations.literal: Most of his writings are not recorded here.
translations.idiomatic: Further compositions are omitted here.

sentences.zh: 籍嘗于蘇門山遇孫登，與商略終古及棲神導氣之術，登皆不應，籍因長嘯而退。

translations.literal: Once on Mount Sumen he met Sun Deng and discussed remote antiquity to the end and the techniques of lodging the spirit and guiding the breath; Deng made no reply at all, so Ruan Ji gave a long whistle and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: On Mount Sumen he met the recluse Sun Deng and debated high antiquity and breath cultivation; Sun Deng never answered, so Ruan Ji gave a long whistle and walked away.

sentences.zh: 至半嶺，聞有聲若鸞鳳之音，響乎岩谷，乃登之嘯也。

translations.literal: Halfway up the slope he heard a sound like the cry of phoenixes, ringing through the cliffs and valleys—it was Deng's whistle.
translations.idiomatic: Halfway down the ridge he heard phoenix-like notes echoing through the peaks—it was Sun Deng answering with a whistle of his own.

sentences.zh: 遂歸著《大人先生傳》，其略曰：「世人所謂君子，惟法是修，惟禮是克。

translations.literal: Thereupon he returned and wrote "Biography of the Great Man," of which the gist runs: "So-called gentlemen of the world cultivate only law and constrain themselves only with ritual.
translations.idiomatic: He then wrote "The Great Gentleman," arguing in essence: "The respectable men of the world polish law, hug ritual,

sentences.zh: 手執圭璧，足履繩墨。

translations.literal: In hand they hold jade tablets; on foot they tread the inked line.
translations.idiomatic: jade tablets in hand, inked guideline underfoot,

sentences.zh: 行欲為目前檢，言欲為無窮則。

translations.literal: In conduct they seek to be an immediate check; in speech they seek to be an endless model.
translations.idiomatic: their deeds a curb on the moment, their words a pattern for all time,

sentences.zh: 少稱鄉黨，長聞鄰國。

translations.literal: In youth they are named in the village association; grown, they are known in neighboring states.
translations.idiomatic: praised in the village as youths, famous abroad as adults,

sentences.zh: 上欲圖三公，下不失九州牧。

translations.literal: Above they aspire to one of the Three Dukes; below they would not miss being shepherd of one of the Nine Regions.
translations.idiomatic: reaching for the Three Excellencies yet never scorning a provincial post.

sentences.zh: 獨不見群虱之處褌中，逃乎深縫，匿乎壞絮，自以為吉宅也。

translations.literal: Alone they do not see how fleas dwell in trousers: they flee into deep seams and hide among rotten padding, thinking they have a lucky dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: They never notice the lice in a pair of pants—cowering in seams and moldy wadding, mistaking filth for a lucky home,

sentences.zh: 行不敢離縫際，動不敢出褌襠，自以為得繩墨也。

translations.literal: In movement they dare not leave the seam's edge; in action they dare not emerge from the trousers' fork, thinking they have got the inked line.
translations.idiomatic: never daring beyond a crease or outside the fly, convinced they are walking straight lines.

sentences.zh: 然炎丘火流，焦邑滅都，群虱處於褌中而不能出也。

translations.literal: Yet when hills of fire flow like flame and towns and capitals are scorched away, the swarm of fleas remains in the trousers and cannot get out.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when wildfire scorches city and plain, those lice stay trapped in the cloth and burn.

sentences.zh: 君子之處域內，何異夫虱之處褌中乎！

translations.literal: A gentleman's dwelling within the bounds of the realm—what difference is there from lice dwelling in trousers!"
translations.idiomatic: What separates a pedant boxed inside the world from a louse boxed inside trousers?"

sentences.zh: 」此亦籍之胸懷本趣也。

translations.literal: This too was the bent of Ruan Ji's own mind.
translations.idiomatic: That parable captured Ruan Ji's own temper.

sentences.zh: 子渾，字長成，有父風。

translations.literal: His son Ruan Hun, courtesy name Changcheng, had his father's manner.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ruan Hun, courtesy name Changcheng, resembled him in spirit.

sentences.zh: 少慕通達，不飾小節。

translations.literal: In youth he admired broad understanding and did not fuss over small points of conduct.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Hun admired breadth of mind and scorned petty scruples.

sentences.zh: 籍謂曰：「仲容已豫吾此流，汝不得復爾！

translations.literal: Ruan Ji told him, "Zhongrong has already joined this current of mine; you must not do so again!"
translations.idiomatic: Ruan Ji warned him, "Your cousin Zhongrong already walks this path with me—you must not follow suit!"

sentences.zh: 」太康中，為太子庶子。

translations.literal: In the Taikang period he served as retainer to the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wu's Taikang era he became a retainer of the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 阮咸字仲容。

translations.literal: Ruan Xian, courtesy name Zhongrong.
translations.idiomatic: Ruan Xian's courtesy name was Zhongrong.

sentences.zh: 父熙，武都太守。

translations.literal: His father Xi was governor of Wudu.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ruan Xi governed Wudu as prefect.

sentences.zh: 咸任達不拘，與叔父籍為竹林之遊，當世禮法者譏其所為。

translations.literal: Xian was broad-minded and unrestrained; with his uncle Ruan Ji he wandered in the Bamboo Grove, and men who upheld ritual of the day condemned their conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Ruan Xian was as free-spirited as his uncle Ruan Ji; together they roamed the Bamboo Grove, drawing scorn from the ritual-minded.

sentences.zh: 咸與籍居道南，諸阮居道北，北阮富而南阮貧。

translations.literal: Ruan Xian dwelled with Ruan Ji south of the lane, while the other Ruans dwelled north of it; the northern Ruans were wealthy and the southern Ruans poor.
translations.idiomatic: He lived south of the lane with Ruan Ji while the rest of the clan lived on the north side—there the rich branch flaunted its wealth and here the poor branch scraped by.

sentences.zh: 七月七日，北阮盛曬衣服，皆錦綺粲目，咸以竿掛大布犢鼻於庭。

translations.literal: On the seventh day of the seventh month the northern Ruans lavishly aired their garments, all brocades dazzling to the eye; Xian hung a large pair of homespun shorts shaped like a calf's nose on a pole in the courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: On the Double Seventh the northerners spread out silks brilliant as jewels; Ruan Xian hoisted a pair of rough cloth shorts on a pole in the yard.

sentences.zh: 人或怪之，答曰：「不能免俗，聊復爾耳！」

translations.literal: Someone thought this strange; he answered, "I cannot escape vulgar custom, so I might as well do the like for a bit!"
translations.idiomatic: When people gawked, he said, "I cannot rise above vulgar ways—so I join them, that is all!"

sentences.zh: 曆仕散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: He served in succession as Gentleman of the Palace Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through appointments as Gentleman of the Palace Gate.

sentences.zh: 山濤舉咸典選，曰：「阮咸貞素寡欲，深識清濁，萬物不能移。

translations.literal: Shan Tao recommended Xian to supervise selection, saying, "Ruan Xian is chaste and plain with few desires, deeply discerning of the clear and the murky—nothing in the world can sway him.
translations.idiomatic: Shan Tao urged his appointment as personnel evaluator: "Ruan Xian is upright, spare in appetite, and reads men with a clear eye—nothing sways him."

sentences.zh: 若在官人之職，必絕于時。

translations.literal: Were he placed in an office that assigns men to posts, he would be unrivaled in his age."
translations.idiomatic: Put him in charge of appointments and he would tower above his generation."

sentences.zh: 」武帝以咸耽酒浮虛，遂不用。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu, because Xian was sunk in wine and empty and frivolous, thereupon did not employ him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu dismissed the idea, judging him a drunkard and a lightweight.

sentences.zh: 太原郭奕高爽有識量，知名于時，少所推先，見咸心醉，不覺歎焉。

translations.literal: Guo Yi of Taiyuan was lofty, frank, perceptive, and generous, renowned in his time, rarely esteeming others ahead of himself; when he saw Xian his heart was intoxicated without his noticing he sighed.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yi of Taiyuan—open, shrewd, and seldom impressed—met Ruan Xian and was utterly won over, sighing before he knew it.

sentences.zh: 而居母喪，縱情越禮。

translations.literal: Yet while mourning for his mother he followed passion and overstepped ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Yet during mourning for his mother he indulged his impulses and flouted ritual.

sentences.zh: 素幸姑之婢，姑當歸于夫家，初雲留婢，既而自從去。

translations.literal: He had long favored his aunt's slave girl; when the aunt was to return to her husband's house she had at first said she would leave the girl behind, but in the end went away with her herself.
translations.idiomatic: He had long desired his aunt's maidservant; the aunt first promised to leave her behind, then took her away when she returned to her husband's house.

sentences.zh: 時方有客，咸聞之，遽借客馬追婢，既及，與婢累騎而還，論者甚非之。

translations.literal: There happened to be a guest present; when Xian heard of it he hastily borrowed the guest's horse to chase the girl; when he caught up with her he rode double with the girl on the return; critics greatly condemned this.
translations.idiomatic: Guests were still in the house when he heard; he borrowed a mount, galloped after the cart, caught the girl, and rode back astride behind her—moralists were scandalized.

sentences.zh: 咸妙解音律，善彈琵琶。

translations.literal: Xian was marvelously skilled at harmonics and good at playing the pipa.
translations.idiomatic: He had a genius for pitch and rhythm and played the pipa to perfection.

sentences.zh: 雖處世不交人事，惟共親知弦歌酣宴而已。

translations.literal: Although he lived in the world and did not deal with human affairs, with close kin alone he would zither, sing, and revel in feasts.
translations.idiomatic: He shunned public life except with family, where he passed nights in song, zither, and wine.

sentences.zh: 與從子脩特相善，每以得意為歡。

translations.literal: With his nephew Ruan Xiu he was especially close, each taking delight in their shared moods.
translations.idiomatic: He was closest to his nephew Ruan Xiu; the two delighted in each other's company.

sentences.zh: 諸阮皆飲酒，咸至，宗人間共集，不復用杯觴斟酌，以大盆盛酒，圓坐相向，大酌更飲。

translations.literal: The Ruans all drank wine; when Xian arrived at a gathering of lineage members they no longer used cups and goblets to pour drinks but filled a great basin with wine, sat in a circle facing one another, and drank in turn by great drafts.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the clan feasted, they set aside cups and ladled wine from a great basin, sitting in a ring and passing it in deep drafts.

sentences.zh: 時有群豕來飲其酒，咸直接去其上，便共飲之。

translations.literal: When a herd of swine came to drink their wine, Xian went straight to their side without driving them off, and then drank together with them.
translations.idiomatic: Pigs wandered up to the wine basin; Ruan Xian sat down among them without shooing them away and shared the drink.

sentences.zh: 群從昆弟莫不以放達為行，籍弗之許。

translations.literal: None of his younger male cousins failed to take wanton abandon as their conduct; Ruan Ji did not approve of this.
translations.idiomatic: Every younger cousin aped his abandon, but Ruan Ji refused to bless their excess.

sentences.zh: 荀勖每與咸論音律，自以為遠不及也，疾之，出補始平太守。

translations.literal: Whenever Xun Xu debated harmonics with Xian he believed himself far inferior, resented him, and sent him out as prefect of Shiping.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Xu, outclassed whenever they discussed music, nursed a grudge and had him posted away as governor of Shiping.

sentences.zh: 以壽終。

translations.literal: He died at his natural span.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his days in old age.

sentences.zh: 二子：瞻、孚。

translations.literal: He had two sons: Zhan and Fu.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Zhan and Fu.

sentences.zh: 瞻字千里。

translations.literal: Zhan, courtesy name Qianli.
translations.idiomatic: Ruan Zhan, courtesy name Qianli,

sentences.zh: 性清虛寡欲，自得於懷。

translations.literal: In nature he was clear, empty, with few desires, finding contentment in his own breast.
translations.idiomatic: was a man of lucid calm and few wants, content within himself.

sentences.zh: 讀書不甚研求，而默識其要，遇理而辯，辭不足而旨有餘。

translations.literal: In reading he did not investigate deeply but silently grasped the essentials; when he encountered a principle he could debate—his words were not ample yet the purport had surplus.
translations.idiomatic: He read without pedantic drilling yet quietly seized essentials; in debate his language was spare but his meaning ran deep.

sentences.zh: 善彈琴，人聞其能，多往求聽，不問貴賤長幼，皆為彈之。

translations.literal: He was skilled at playing the zither; people who heard of his ability often went to ask to listen, and regardless of noble or base, elder or younger, he would play for them.
translations.idiomatic: He played the zither beautifully, and whoever came—high or low, old or young—he would play for.

sentences.zh: 神氣沖和，而不知向人所在。

translations.literal: His spirit and bearing were mild and harmonious, and one did not know where he turned his attention toward others.
translations.idiomatic: His manner was gentle and diffuse; you could never tell where his mind had drifted.

sentences.zh: 內兄潘岳每令鼓琴，終日達夜，無忤色。

translations.literal: His wife's brother Pan Yue often had him strum the zither from dawn through night without showing annoyance.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Yue, his brother-in-law, kept him playing from dusk till dawn, yet he never showed irritation.

sentences.zh: 由是識者歎其恬澹，不可榮辱矣。

translations.literal: For this reason those who knew him sighed at his tranquillity and plainness—he could not be moved by glory or disgrace.
translations.idiomatic: Observers marveled at his equipoise: neither honor nor shame could touch him.

sentences.zh: 舉止灼然。

translations.literal: In bearing he was clear and settled.
translations.idiomatic: In deportment he was luminous and composed.

sentences.zh: 見司徒王戎，戎問曰：「聖人貴名教，老莊明自然，其旨同異？

translations.literal: When he saw Minister of Education Wang Rong, Rong asked, "The sages prized name and teaching; Laozi and Zhuangzi clarified spontaneity of nature—are their aims the same or different?"
translations.idiomatic: Visiting Minister of Education Wang Rong, he was asked whether the sages' esteem for moral norms and Laozi-Zhuang's teaching of spontaneity meant the same thing or not.

sentences.zh: 」瞻曰：「將無同。

translations.literal: Zhan replied, "I suppose they are not different."
translations.idiomatic: Ruan Zhan answered, "I should think they are not unlike each other."

sentences.zh: 」戎咨嗟良久，即命辟之。

translations.literal: Rong sighed in admiration a long time, then ordered him summoned to office.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Rong mused at length, then ordered him offered a post on the spot.

sentences.zh: 時人謂之「三語掾」。

translations.literal: People of the time called him the "clerk in three sentences."
translations.idiomatic: Wits dubbed him the "three-line secretary."

sentences.zh: 太尉王衍亦雅重之。

translations.literal: Grand Commandant Wang Yan also thought highly of him.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commandant Wang Yan likewise esteemed him.

sentences.zh: 瞻嘗群行，冒熱渴甚，逆旅有井，眾人競趨之，瞻獨逡巡在後，須飲者畢乃進，其夷退無競如此。

translations.literal: Zhan once traveled in a group, sweltering and very thirsty; at an inn there was a well and everyone raced thereto, but Zhan alone loitered behind and only advanced when those who wished to drink had finished—such was his yielding withdrawal without contention.
translations.idiomatic: On a sweltering journey the party rushed a roadside well; Ruan Zhan hung back until every thirst was slaked—so unhurried and ungrasping was he.

sentences.zh: 東海王越鎮許昌，以瞻為記室參軍，與王承、謝鯤、鄧攸俱在越府。

translations.literal: Prince of the East Sea Sima Yue garrisoned Xuchang and appointed Zhan secretary in his headquarters, with Wang Cheng, Xie Kun, and Deng You together in Yue's bureau.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Yue, Prince of the East Sea, held Xuchang, he named Ruan Zhan secretary-adjutant alongside Wang Cheng, Xie Kun, and Deng You.

sentences.zh: 越與瞻等書曰：「禮，年八歲出就外傅，明始可以加師訓之則；

translations.literal: Yue wrote to Zhan and the others saying, "By ritual, at eight years one goes out to the external tutor, meaning one can thereupon receive the model admonitions of a teacher;
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yue wrote: "Ritual says a boy of eight leaves home for outer schooling, ready for a teacher's discipline;

sentences.zh: 十年曰幼學，明可漸先王之教也。

translations.literal: at ten one is called 'child learning,' meaning one may gradually receive the teachings of former kings.
translations.idiomatic: at ten he enters 'child study' and may absorb the lessons of the ancient kings.

sentences.zh: 然學之所入淺，體之所安深。

translations.literal: Yet what study ingests is shallow, what embodiment settles is deep.
translations.idiomatic: Yet book learning stays shallow; what shapes the person runs deeper.

sentences.zh: 是以閑習禮容，不如式瞻儀度；

translations.literal: Therefore leisurely practice of ritual demeanor is not as good as personally viewing deportment and measure;
translations.idiomatic: So rehearsing ritual gestures counts for less than watching true bearing in action;

sentences.zh: 諷誦遺言，不若親承音旨。

translations.literal: chanting handed-down sayings is not as good as receiving in person tone and intent.
translations.idiomatic: reciting old texts counts for less than hearing a living voice explain them.

sentences.zh: 小兒毗既無令淑之質，不聞道德之風，望諸君時以閑豫，周旋誨接。」

translations.literal: My young son Pi possesses neither fine and excellent endowment nor has he heard the breeze of the Way and virtue; I look to you gentlemen, whenever you are at leisure, to move among him and instruct him in conversation."
translations.idiomatic: My boy Pi lacks natural grace and has felt little of the Way; when you are free, move with him and teach him in conversation."

sentences.zh: 永嘉中，為太子舍人。

translations.literal: In the Yongjia era he served as retainer attendant to the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongjia he became attendant for the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 瞻素執無鬼論，物莫能難，每自謂此理足可以辯正幽明。

translations.literal: Zhan always held a doctrine that there are no ghosts—no one could refute him, and he often claimed this principle surely could settle the debate between hidden and manifest.
translations.idiomatic: He was famous for arguing there are no ghosts; none could overturn him, and he boasted the point settled spirit against flesh.

sentences.zh: 忽有一客通名詣瞻，寒溫畢，聊談名理。

translations.literal: Suddenly there was a visitor who announced his name and paid a visit to Zhan; after amenities he idly discussed abstract principle.
translations.idiomatic: A stranger announced himself, exchanged courtesies, and drifted into metaphysical talk.

sentences.zh: 客甚有才辯，瞻與之言，良久及鬼神之事，反覆甚苦。

translations.literal: The visitor was very talented at disputation; Zhan spoke with him at length until they reached the matter of ghosts and spirits, arguing back and forth with great vexation.
translations.idiomatic: He was brilliant in debate; they wrangled for hours until the talk turned to ghosts, growing fierce.

sentences.zh: 客遂屈，乃作色曰：「鬼神，古今聖賢所共傳，君何得獨言無！

translations.literal: The visitor was at last worsted, then changed color and said, "Ghosts and spirits are passed down alike by sages ancient and modern—how can you alone say they do not exist!
translations.idiomatic: At last the visitor flushed and said, "Sages old and new all attest spirits—how dare you deny them!

sentences.zh: 即僕便是鬼。

translations.literal: As for myself, I am a ghost."
translations.idiomatic: I myself am a ghost."

sentences.zh: 」於是變為異形，須臾消滅。

translations.literal: Thereupon he changed into a strange form and in a moment vanished.
translations.idiomatic: He shifted into a monstrous shape and vanished in an instant.

sentences.zh: 瞻默然，意色大惡。

translations.literal: Zhan was silent; his expression was greatly disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: Ruan Zhan sat speechless, his face gone gray.

sentences.zh: 後歲餘，病卒於倉垣，時年三十。

translations.literal: After more than a year he died of illness at Cangyuan, aged thirty.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he died of illness at Cangyuan, only thirty years old.

sentences.zh: 孚字遙集。

translations.literal: Fu, courtesy name Yaoji.
translations.idiomatic: Ruan Fu, courtesy name Yaoji,

sentences.zh: 其母，即胡婢也。

translations.literal: His mother was a Hu slave girl.
translations.idiomatic: was born to a Hu bondwoman.

sentences.zh: 孚之初生，其姑取王延壽《魯靈光殿賦》曰「胡人遙集於上楹」而以字焉。

translations.literal: When Fu was born, his aunt took the line from Wang Yanshou's "Rhapsody on the Hall of Numen Light in Lu," "The Hu from afar gather at the upper tie-beam," and gave him a name from it.
translations.idiomatic: His aunt, quoting Wang Yanshou's rhapsody on the Hall of Spiritual Light in Lu—where barbarians "gather from afar beneath the ridgepole"—chose his name from those words.

sentences.zh: 初辟太傅府，遷騎兵屬。

translations.literal: At first he was summoned to the Grand Tutor's office, then promoted to aide in the cavalry command.
translations.idiomatic: He began in the Grand Tutor's bureau and moved up to aide in the cavalry service.

sentences.zh: 避亂渡江，元帝以為安東參軍。

translations.literal: Fleeing turmoil he crossed the river; Emperor Yuan appointed him adjutant to the general pacifying the east.
translations.idiomatic: Crossing the Yangzi ahead of the collapse, he became adjutant to the eastern pacification command under Emperor Yuan.

sentences.zh: 蓬髮飲酒，不以王務嬰心。

translations.literal: With tangled hair he drank wine and did not let state business encumber his mind.
translations.idiomatic: He drank with hair uncombed and refused to let paperwork weigh on him.

sentences.zh: 時帝既用申、韓以救世，而孚之徒未能棄也。

translations.literal: At the time the emperor had already applied Shen Buhai and Han Fei to save the age, yet men such as Fu could not cast them aside.
translations.idiomatic: The court was applying Legalist rigor to save the realm, yet men of Ruan Fu's stamp could not simply vanish.

sentences.zh: 雖然，不以事任處之。

translations.literal: Even so, he did not entrust them with substantive duties.
translations.idiomatic: Still, he kept them away from real responsibility.

sentences.zh: 轉丞相從事中郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to gentleman of the staff in the Chancellor's service.
translations.idiomatic: Ruan Fu was shifted to aide in the chancellery.

sentences.zh: 終日酣縱，恆為有司所按，帝每優容之。

translations.literal: All day he drank wildly and was constantly impeached by the authorities, yet the emperor always treated him with indulgent tolerance.
translations.idiomatic: He caroused endlessly and was repeatedly censored, but the emperor indulged him.

sentences.zh: 琅邪王裒為車騎將軍，鎮廣陵，高選綱佐，以孚為長史。

translations.literal: Wang Ai of Langye was chariot-and-cavalry general garrisoning Guangling, selecting high-ranking assistants strictly, and appointed Fu chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ai of Langye, chariot-and-cavalry general at Guangling, was picking elite staff and chose Ruan Fu as chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 帝謂曰：「卿既統軍府，郊壘多事，宜節飲也。

translations.literal: The emperor said to him, "You now command the military headquarters; the camp outer suburbs have many affairs—you ought to moderate your drinking."
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign told him, "You head an army headquarters on a busy frontier—you should drink less."

sentences.zh: 」孚答曰：「陛下不以臣不才，委之以戎旅之重。

translations.literal: Fu replied, "Your Majesty, not deeming your subject lacking in talent, has entrusted him with the heavy burden of the army.
translations.idiomatic: Ruan Fu replied, "You burden a dullard like me with military weight."

sentences.zh: 臣僶勉從事，不敢有言者，竊以今王蒞鎮，威風赫然，皇澤遐被，賊寇斂跡，氛昆既澄，日月自朗，臣亦何可爵火不息？

translations.literal: Your subject strains to carry out the work and dares not speak up only because, in his humble view, now that Your Majesty's prince has taken up residence in the commandery, his awe-inspiring power spreads far, imperial grace reaches to a distance, bandit hosts draw in their tracks, foul vapors are already clear, sun and moon shine of themselves—why should your subject be 'fire on the torch' without cease?
translations.idiomatic: I would have kept silent save for this: your prince's presence makes terror spread and imperial grace reach far—foes shrink, the air clears, sun and moon seem brighter—why should I still fuss like a torch flame that will not die?

sentences.zh: 正應端拱嘯詠，以樂當年耳。

translations.literal: I ought instead to fold my hands, whistle, and chant poetry to enjoy these years."
translations.idiomatic: Better I fold my hands, whistle, and enjoy my years in peace."

sentences.zh: 」遷黃門侍郎、散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Gentleman in the Yellow Gate, Regular Cavalier Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced to Gentleman at the Yellow Gate and Regular Cavalier Attendant.

sentences.zh: 嘗以金貂換酒，復為所司彈劾，帝宥之。

translations.literal: Once he exchanged a gold marten tail for wine and again was impeached by the authorities; the emperor forgave him.
translations.idiomatic: He once traded a gold sable tail for wine, drew another impeachment, and was pardoned.

sentences.zh: 轉太子中庶子、左衛率，領屯騎校尉。

translations.literal: He was transferred to retainer to the heir apparent, leader of the guards of the left, concurrently colonel of the garrison cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was retainer to the crown prince, leader of the left guards, and colonel of garrison cavalry.

sentences.zh: 明帝即位，遷侍中。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming came to the throne he was promoted to palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming raised him to palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 從平王敦，賜爵南安縣侯。

translations.literal: He accompanied the pacification of Wang Dun and was enfeoffed as marquis of Nan'an county.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the campaign against Wang Dun and was enfeoffed marquis of Nan'an.

sentences.zh: 轉吏部尚書，領東海王師，稱疾不拜。

translations.literal: He was transferred to minister of the Ministry of Appointments, concurrently tutor to the Prince of the East Sea, but pleaded illness and did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: He was named minister of personnel and tutor to the Prince of the East Sea but pleaded illness and stayed home.

sentences.zh: 詔就家用之，尚書令郗鑒以為非禮。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that he be employed at home; minister of the left Chi Jian deemed this contrary to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered him employed from his house; Chi Jian, minister of the left, called that improper.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「就用之誠不快，不爾便廢才。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Employing him at home is indeed not satisfactory; if not so, one would waste his talent."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor answered, "It is awkward, yes—but otherwise his talent goes unused."

sentences.zh: 」及帝疾大漸，溫嶠入受顧命，過孚，要與同行。

translations.literal: When the emperor's illness grew critically grave, Wen Jiao entered to receive the testamentary charge; passing Fu he invited him to go together.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor sank toward death, Wen Jiao came to take the deathbed charge and invited Ruan Fu into the carriage.

sentences.zh: 升車，乃告之曰：「主上遂大漸，江左危弱，實資群賢，共康世務。

translations.literal: When they mounted the carriage he told him, "The sovereign has at last grown desperately ill; east of the Yangzi is frail and weak; it truly depends on worthy men together to bring world affairs to good order.
translations.idiomatic: Wen said, "The throne is failing; the southland is weak—we need worthy men to steady the realm.

sentences.zh: 卿時望所歸，今欲屈卿同受顧托。

translations.literal: You are whom the age looks to; now I wish to trouble you to receive together the testamentary entrustment."
translations.idiomatic: You command respect; I want you beside me to accept the regency."

sentences.zh: 」孚不答，固求下車，嶠不許。

translations.literal: Fu did not answer but firmly asked to get down from the carriage; Jiao did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Ruan Fu said nothing, demanded to be let off, and Wen Jiao refused.

sentences.zh: 垂至台門，告嶠內迫，求暫下，便徒步還家。

translations.literal: As they drew near the Terrace gate he told Jiao he was pressed inside and begged briefly to get down, then on foot returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Near the palace gate he pleaded a call of nature, slipped down, and walked home.

sentences.zh: 初，祖約性好財，孚性好屐，同是累而未判其得失。

translations.literal: At first Zu Yue by nature loved wealth, Fu by nature loved clogs—both were obsessions yet people had not decided which was worse or better.
translations.idiomatic: People once compared Zu Yue's greed for money with Ruan Fu's passion for wooden clogs—two manias, hard to rank.

sentences.zh: 有詣約，見正料財物，客至，屏當不盡，餘兩小簏，以著背後，傾身障之，意未能平。

translations.literal: Someone visited Yue and saw him tallying goods; when the guest arrived he had not finished putting screens away; two small baskets remained which he placed behind his back, bending his body to shield them, his mind still unsteady.
translations.idiomatic: A caller on Zu Yue found him counting coin; startled mid-task, he hid two small chests behind his back, hunched and uneasy.

sentences.zh: 或有詣阮，正見自蠟屐，因自歎曰：「未知一生當著幾量屐！

translations.literal: Or someone visited Ruan and saw him rubbing clogs with his own hand waxing them, whereupon he sighed to himself, "I do not know in one life how many pairs of clogs I shall wear!"
translations.idiomatic: A caller on Ruan Fu found him waxing clogs and sighing, "Who knows how many pairs I'll wear in one lifetime?"

sentences.zh: 」神色甚閑暢。

translations.literal: His expression and bearing were very easy and genial.
translations.idiomatic: His face stayed serene and bright.

sentences.zh: 於是勝負始分。

translations.literal: Thereupon winners and losers were first distinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Then everyone knew which obsession was nobler.

sentences.zh: 咸和初，拜丹陰尹。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianhe he was appointed governor of Danyin.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Xianhe he became governor of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 時太后臨朝，政出舅族。

translations.literal: At the time the empress dowager faced the court and government issued from her maternal uncles' kin.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager ruled from behind the screen while her uncles pulled the strings.

sentences.zh: 孚謂所親曰：「今江東雖累世，而年數實淺。

translations.literal: Fu told those close to him, "Although east of the Yangzi has lasted many generations, in years of count it is in truth shallow.
translations.idiomatic: Ruan Fu told friends, "This southern court may boast many reigns, but its calendar is still short.

sentences.zh: 主幼時艱，運終百六，而庾亮年少，德信未孚，以吾觀之，將兆亂矣。

translations.literal: The ruler is young and the times are hard; the cycle has reached its 'hundred-six' ill-omened span, yet Yu Liang is young in years, his virtue and trust not yet winning confidence—in my view portents of disorder will appear."
translations.idiomatic: The boy emperor faces a hard age; the 'hundred-and-six' ill cycle nears; Yu Liang is young, untested, untrusted—I see the makings of chaos."

sentences.zh: 」會廣州刺史劉顗卒，遂苦求出。

translations.literal: It happened that the inspector of Guangzhou Liu Kai died, so he urgently begged to go out on assignment.
translations.idiomatic: When Guangzhou inspector Liu Kai died, he begged desperately for an outside post.

sentences.zh: 王導等以孚疏放，非京尹才，乃除都督交、廣、寧三州軍事、鎮南將軍、領平越中郎將、廣州刺史、假節。

translations.literal: Wang Dao and others, because Fu was reckless and dissolute, not having talent for capital governor, thereupon appointed him military overseer of Jiao, Guang, and Ning three provinces, general who guards the south, concurrently colonel chastising the Yue, inspector of Guangzhou, with credential baton.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dao judged him unfit for the capital magistracy but named him military commander over Jiao, Guang, and Ning, general who guards the south, colonel against the Yue, inspector of Guangzhou—with plenipotentiary baton.

sentences.zh: 未至鎮，卒，年四十九。

translations.literal: Before he reached his command he died, aged forty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died en route, forty-nine years old.

sentences.zh: 尋而蘇峻作逆，識者以為知幾。

translations.literal: Soon Su Jun rebelled; those discerning thought he had known the subtle turning.
translations.idiomatic: When Su Jun rose soon after, wise men said he had read the signs.

sentences.zh: 無子，從孫廣嗣。

translations.literal: He had no sons; his younger brother's grandson Ruan Guang inherited.
translations.idiomatic: Childless, he passed his line to a grandnephew, Ruan Guang.

sentences.zh: 修字宣子。

translations.literal: Xiu, courtesy name Xuanzi.
translations.idiomatic: Ruan Xiu, courtesy name Xuanzi.

sentences.zh: 好《易》《老》，善清言。

translations.literal: He loved the Changes and Laozi and was good at Pure Conversation.
translations.idiomatic: He loved the Zhouyi and Laozi and excelled at qingtan.

sentences.zh: 嘗有論鬼神有無者，皆以人死者有鬼，修獨以為無，曰：「今見鬼者雲著生時衣服，若人死有鬼，衣服有鬼邪？

translations.literal: Once there was a debate on whether ghosts exist; all held that when men die there are ghosts; Xiu alone thought there were none, saying, "Those who claim to see ghosts say they wear the clothes they had in life—if when men die there are ghosts, do clothes have ghosts too?"
translations.idiomatic: In a debate on ghosts everyone assumed the dead lingered; Ruan Xiu alone denied it: "Witnesses say ghosts wear their living clothes—if the dead have ghosts, do garments have ghosts too?"

sentences.zh: 」論者服焉。

translations.literal: The debaters conceded.
translations.idiomatic: The others conceded the point.

sentences.zh: 後遂伐社樹，或止之，修曰：「若社而為樹，伐樹則社移；

translations.literal: Later he thereupon cut down the altar tree of the local earth god; someone tried to stop him; Xiu said, "If the earth god is identified with a tree, then cutting the tree removes the altar;
translations.idiomatic: Later he chopped down a village earth-god's tree; when warned, he said, "If the god is the tree, felling it moves the shrine;

sentences.zh: 樹而為社，伐樹則社亡矣。」

translations.literal: If it is a tree made into the earth god, then cutting the tree destroys the earth god."
translations.idiomatic: if the tree is the god, then cutting it ends the god."

sentences.zh: 性簡任，不修人事。

translations.literal: He was plain and easygoing in nature and did not cultivate human dealings.
translations.idiomatic: He was blunt and easygoing and kept no social façade.

sentences.zh: 絕不喜見俗人，遇便舍去。

translations.literal: He utterly disliked meeting vulgar people; when he encountered them he would leave at once.
translations.idiomatic: He detested philistines and would bolt the moment he met one.

sentences.zh: 意有所思，率爾褰裳，不避晨夕，至或無言，但欣然相對。

translations.literal: When his mind was on something he would abruptly hitch up his robes without regard to dawn or dusk; sometimes they reached the point of uttering no word but only gazing at each other with delight.
translations.idiomatic: When a thought seized him he would hike his skirts and go, heedless of hour; sometimes he and a companion sat in wordless, happy understanding.

sentences.zh: 常步行，以百錢掛杖頭，至酒店，便獨酣暢。

translations.literal: He habitually walked with a hundred cash hung on his staff head; when he reached a wine shop he would alone drink his fill.
translations.idiomatic: He walked with coins strung on his staff, slipped into taverns, and drank alone to blissful excess.

sentences.zh: 雖當世富貴而不肯顧，家無儋石之儲，宴如也。

translations.literal: Although there were the rich and noble of his age he would not deign to look toward them; his house held no store of a picul or stone of grain, yet he was easy as at a feast.
translations.idiomatic: He scorned the rich and powerful of the day, yet though his larder held not a peck of grain he lived as serenely as if at banquet.

sentences.zh: 與兄弟同志，常自得于林阜之間。

translations.literal: With his brothers he shared the same aim and often found contentment among woods and hills.
translations.idiomatic: He and his brothers shared one mind and took quiet joy in hills and streams.

sentences.zh: 王衍當時談宗，自以論《易》略盡，然有所未了，研之終莫悟，每云「不知比沒當見能通之者不」。

translations.literal: Wang Yan at the time was patriarch of talk; he believed he had nearly exhausted discourse on the Changes, yet something remained unfathomed that he studied to the end without awakening, and he often said, "I do not know before I die whether I shall see anyone who can penetrate it."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan headed the pure-talk circles, thought he had plumbed the Zhouyi yet still sensed a blind spot he could not crack, and muttered, "Will I live to meet anyone who truly masters it?"

sentences.zh: 衍族子敦謂衍曰：「阮宣子可與言。

translations.literal: Yan's clansman Dun said to Yan, "Ruan Xuanzi can be spoken with."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun told Wang Yan, "You can actually talk ideas with Ruan Xiu."

sentences.zh: 」衍曰：「吾亦聞之，但未知其亹癖之處定何如耳！

translations.literal: Yan said, "I have heard that too, but I do not yet know wherein his obsessive bent certainly lies!"
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan answered, "I have heard the same—but where lies his real obsession?"

sentences.zh: 」及與修談，言寡而旨暢，衍乃嘆服焉。

translations.literal: When he actually spoke with Xiu, Xiu's words were few yet his purport fluent, whereupon Yan sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Their conversation proved Xiu spare of phrase but lucid in meaning, and Wang Yan cried out in admiration.

sentences.zh: 梁國張偉志趣不常，自隱于屠釣，修愛其才美，而知其不真。

translations.literal: Zhang Wei of Liang had uncommon aims and had hidden himself among butchers and anglers; Xiu loved his talent and appearance but knew him inauthentic.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wei of Liang was odd in aspiration and posed as a butcher-angler recluse; Ruan Xiu admired his gifts yet sensed the pose was hollow.

sentences.zh: 偉後為黃門郎、陳留內史，果以世事受累。

translations.literal: Wei later became Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and interior secretary of Chenliu, and indeed was entangled by worldly affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wei later rose to Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and interior secretary of Chenliu and, as Xiu foresaw, was ruined by politics.

sentences.zh: 修居貧，年四十餘未有室，王敦等斂錢為婚，皆名士也，時慕之者求入錢而不得。

translations.literal: Xiu lived in poverty; past forty he still had no wife, whereupon Wang Dun and others collected money for a wedding—all were famed scholars; those who admired the moment begged to contribute money but could not.
translations.idiomatic: Ruan Xiu stayed poor and unmarried past forty, so Wang Dun and other luminaries pooled a bride-price; hangers-on who craved the cachet were refused a share.

sentences.zh: 修所著述甚寡，嘗作《大鵬贊》曰：「蒼蒼大鵬，誕自北溟。

translations.literal: Xiu's writings were very few; he once composed "Rhapsody on the Great Peng" saying: "Vast is the great peng, born in the northern dark."
translations.idiomatic: He wrote little; among his pieces is a "Rhapsody on the Great Peng" that opens: "Darkly vast, the great peng, conceived in the Northern Dark."

sentences.zh: 假精靈鱗，神化以生。

translations.literal: Borrowing the seminal essence of scale and fin, by spirit-transformation it came into life.
translations.idiomatic: It draws life from the subtle essences of scale and fin, born of spirit-transformation.

sentences.zh: 如雲之翼，如山之形。

translations.literal: Its wings are like clouds, its form like mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Its wings veil the sky like clouds; its bulk looms like a mountain.

sentences.zh: 海運水擊，扶搖上征。

translations.literal: When the sea rolls and waves strike, it mounts the whirlwind on high.
translations.idiomatic: When seas shift and surge strikes, it rides the whirlwind upward.

sentences.zh: 翕然層舉，背負太清。

translations.literal: With one gulp it layers its ascent, bearing the Grand Pure on its back.
translations.idiomatic: In one soaring burst it climbs tier on tier, shouldering the empyrean.

sentences.zh: 志存天地，不屑唐庭。

translations.literal: Its will lodges in heaven and earth; it disdains the court of Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Its purpose spans heaven and earth; it scorns the halls of Tang.

sentences.zh: 鴬鳩仰笑，尺鷃所輕。

translations.literal: The oriole and dove laugh looking up; the inch-long quail holds it light.
translations.idiomatic: Warbler and dove titter upward; the inch-long quail sneers.

sentences.zh: 超世高逝，莫知其情。」

translations.literal: It leaves the world on high and vanishes; none know its true heart."
translations.idiomatic: It quits the vulgar world and soars away—none can fathom its heart."

sentences.zh: 王敦時為鴻臚卿，謂修曰：「卿常無食，鴻臚丞差有祿，能作不？

translations.literal: Wang Dun at the time was chamberlain for ceremonials; he said to Xiu, "You often lack food; the assistant chamberlain post carries a salary—could you take it?"
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun, then chamberlain for ceremonials, said, "You are always hungry—the assistant chamberlain has a stipend; will you take it?"

sentences.zh: 」修曰：「亦復可爾耳！

translations.literal: Xiu said, "That too could be done."
translations.idiomatic: Ruan Xiu said, "I suppose I could manage that."

sentences.zh: 」遂為之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he took it.
translations.idiomatic: So he accepted the post.

sentences.zh: 轉太傅行參軍、太子洗馬。

translations.literal: He was transferred adjutant acting for the Grand Tutor, groom launderer to the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He moved on to acting adjutant to the Grand Tutor and groom-launderer to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 避亂南行，至西陽期思縣，為賊所害，時年四十二。

translations.literal: Fleeing turmoil he went south and reached Qisi county in Xiyang, where robbers killed him; he was forty-two years old.
translations.idiomatic: Fleeing war southward he reached Qisi in Xiyang, where bandits cut him down at the age of forty-two.

sentences.zh: 放字思度。

translations.literal: Fang, courtesy name Sidu.
translations.idiomatic: Ruan Fang, courtesy name Sidu,

sentences.zh: 祖略，齊郡太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather was Lue, governor of Qi commandery.
translations.idiomatic: his grandfather Ruan Lue governed Qi commandery,

sentences.zh: 父顗，淮南內史。

translations.literal: His father was Kai, interior secretary of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: his father Ruan Kai was interior secretary of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 放少與孚並知名。

translations.literal: Fang in youth was as renowned as Ruan Fu.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he matched Ruan Fu in reputation.

sentences.zh: 中興，除太學博士、太子中舍人、庶子。

translations.literal: At the restoration he was appointed erudite of the academy, attendant of the household to the heir apparent, and retainer.
translations.idiomatic: After the Eastern Jin restoration he became academy erudite, household attendant to the heir apparent, and palace retainer.

sentences.zh: 時雖戎車屢駕，而放侍太子，常說《老》《莊》，不及軍國。

translations.literal: Although war chariots set out repeatedly, Fang while attending the heir apparent constantly expounded Laozi and Zhuangzi and never touched military or state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Though armies marched again and again, he tutored the heir only in Laozi and Zhuangzi, never touching strategy or policy.

sentences.zh: 明帝甚友愛之。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming was very friendly and fond of him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming treated him as an intimate friend.

sentences.zh: 轉黃門侍郎，遷吏部郎，在銓管之任，甚有稱績。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, then promoted to director in the Ministry of Appointments; in the office that wielded evaluation he had very praised achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and then personnel director, he won praise for even-handed appointments.

sentences.zh: 時成帝幼沖，庾氏執政，放求為交州，乃除監交州軍事、揚威將軍、交州刺史。

translations.literal: At the time Emperor Cheng was in minority and the Yu clan held power; Fang begged for Jiaozhou, and was therefore appointed overseer of military affairs in Jiaozhou, general who displays might, inspector of Jiaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Cheng was a child and the Yu clan ran the court, Ruan Fang begged for distant Jiaozhou and received the posts of military overseer, General Who Displays Might, and inspector.

sentences.zh: 行達甯浦，逢陶侃將高寶平梁碩自交州還，放設饌請寶，伏兵殺之。

translations.literal: On the road he reached Ningpu and met the general Gao Bao of Tao Kan's command returning from leveling Liang Shuo in Jiaozhou; Fang set a feast to invite Bao and ambushed soldiers who slew him.
translations.idiomatic: Near Ningpu he met Tao Kan's officer Gao Bao returning from crushing Liang Shuo; Ruan Fang feasted him, then had him ambushed and killed.

sentences.zh: 寶眾擊放，敗走，保簡陽城，得免。

translations.literal: Bao's troops attacked Fang; he was defeated and fled, defended Jianyang city, and escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Bao's men counterattacked; Ruan Fang fled and holed up in Jianyang until the storm passed.

sentences.zh: 到州少時，暴發渴，見寶為祟，遂卒，朝廷甚悼惜之，年四十四。

translations.literal: Shortly after reaching his province he suddenly developed unquenchable thirst, saw Bao as a haunting spirit, and thereupon died; the court deeply regretted him; he was forty-four.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after taking up his post he was seized by raging thirst, saw Gao Bao's ghost, and died; the court mourned him deeply—he was forty-four.

sentences.zh: 追贈廷尉。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was given minister of justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 放素知名，而性清約，不營產業，為吏部郎，不免饑寒。

translations.literal: Fang had long been renowned yet his nature was clear and spare; he did not build estates, and as director in the Ministry of Appointments could not avoid cold and hunger.
translations.idiomatic: Famous yet frugal, he built no fortune; even as personnel chief he shivered and hungered.

sentences.zh: 王導、庾亮以其名士，常供給衣食。

translations.literal: Wang Dao and Yu Liang, because he was a famous scholar, constantly supplied clothing and food.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dao and Yu Liang kept him clothed and fed out of respect for his name.

sentences.zh: 子晞之，南頓太守。

translations.literal: His son was Xizhi, governor of Nandun.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ruan Xizhi became governor of Nandun.

sentences.zh: 裕字思曠。

translations.literal: Yu, courtesy name Sikuang.
translations.idiomatic: Ruan Yu, courtesy name Sikuang,

sentences.zh: 宏達不及放，而以德業知名。

translations.literal: In broad magnanimity he did not match Fang, yet by virtue and enterprise he was renowned.
translations.idiomatic: lacked Ruan Fang's dash but surpassed him in moral repute.

sentences.zh: 弱冠辟太宰掾。

translations.literal: At the capping he was summoned clerk to the grand steward.
translations.idiomatic: At his capping he entered service as clerk to the grand steward.

sentences.zh: 大將軍王敦命為主簿，甚被知遇。

translations.literal: Grand General Wang Dun ordered him chief clerk and greatly favored him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun, grand general, made him chief clerk and doted on him.

sentences.zh: 裕以敦有不臣之心，乃終日酣觴，以酒廢職。

translations.literal: Yu because Dun harbored a subject's breach of loyalty thereupon drank deep all day and used wine to ruin his office duties.
translations.idiomatic: Sensing Wang Dun's treasonous ambition, Ruan Yu drank all day and feigned incompetence.

sentences.zh: 敦謂裕非當世實才，徒有虛譽而已，出為溧陽令，復以公事免官。

translations.literal: Dun deemed Yu no practical talent of the age, only empty reputation, and sent him out as magistrate of Liyang; again he was dismissed from office for a public matter.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun wrote him off as a hollow reputation and packed him off to Liyang county, then dismissed him on a bureaucratic pretext.

sentences.zh: 由是得違敦難，論者以此貴之。

translations.literal: By this means he escaped Dun's disaster, and commentators on that account esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: Thus he slipped Wang Dun's purge, and wise men praised the stratagem.

sentences.zh: 咸和初，除尚書郎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianhe he was appointed Gentleman of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: At Xianhe's opening he was named Gentleman of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 時事故之後，公私弛廢，裕遂去職還家，居會稽剡縣。

translations.literal: At the time after troubles public and private were lax and ruined; Yu thereupon left office and returned home, dwelling in Shan county of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: With the realm still broken after rebellion, he resigned and retired to Shan in Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 司徒王導引為從事中郎，固辭不就。

translations.literal: Minister of Education Wang Dao summoned him as gentleman of the staff but he firmly declined and did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dao summoned him as staff adviser; he refused flatly.

sentences.zh: 朝廷將欲征之，裕知不得已，乃求為王舒撫軍長史。

translations.literal: When the court was about to summon him, Yu knowing he could not refuse begged instead to serve as chief clerk to Wang Shu's army of consolation.
translations.idiomatic: When fresh summons loomed, he begged instead for chief clerk under Wang Shu's pacification command—anything to stay clear of the capital.

sentences.zh: 舒薨，除吏部郎，不就。

translations.literal: When Shu died he was appointed director in the Ministry of Appointments but did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Shu died he was offered the personnel ministry and again declined.

sentences.zh: 即家拜臨海太守，少時去職。

translations.literal: He was invested at his home as governor of Linhai, and after a short time left office.
translations.idiomatic: The court invested him governor of Linhai from his home; he quit within months.

sentences.zh: 司空郗鑒請為長史，詔征秘書監，皆以疾辭。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Chi Jian requested him as chief clerk; an edict summoned him as director of the palace library; all he declined citing illness.
translations.idiomatic: Chi Jian wanted him as chief clerk; an edict named him palace librarian—each time he pleaded illness.

sentences.zh: 復除東陽太守。

translations.literal: Again he was appointed governor of Dongyang.
translations.idiomatic: He briefly served as governor of Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 尋征侍中，不就。

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned palace attendant but did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: Palace attendant was next offered; he never appeared.

sentences.zh: 還剡山，有肥遁之志。

translations.literal: He returned to Mount Shan with a mind to lofty reclusion.
translations.idiomatic: He withdrew to Mount Shan, intent on high reclusion.

sentences.zh: 有以問王羲之，羲之曰：「此公近不驚寵辱，雖古之沈冥，何以過此！

translations.literal: Someone asked Wang Xizhi about him; Xizhi said, "This gentleman lately is not stirred by favor or disgrace—even the hidden ones of antiquity—how could they surpass this!"
translations.idiomatic: Asked for a verdict, Wang Xizhi said, "He is proof against glory and shame—who among the ancient recluses surpasses him?"

sentences.zh: 」人云，裕骨氣不及逸少，簡秀不如真長，韶潤不如仲祖，思致不如殷浩，而兼有諸人之美。

translations.literal: People said Yu's bone and spirit did not match Yixuan, his spare elegance did not match Zhenchang, his polish did not match Zhongzu, his thought reach did not match Yin Hao, yet he combined the beauties of them all.
translations.idiomatic: Gossip compared him to Wang Xizhi, Liu Tan, Wang Shu, and Yin Hao—falling short in each trait yet somehow blending their virtues.

sentences.zh: 成帝崩，裕赴山陵，事畢便還。

translations.literal: When Emperor Cheng died, Yu went to the tumulus mountains; when the affair was finished he returned at once.
translations.idiomatic: At Emperor Cheng's funeral he rode to the mausoleum and bolted the moment rites ended.

sentences.zh: 諸人相與追之，裕亦審時流必當逐己，而疾去，至方山不相及。

translations.literal: All pursued him together; Yu also judged that the fashionable set would certainly pursue him, and therefore left swiftly; they did not overtake him by Mount Fangshan.
translations.idiomatic: The salon raced after him; foreseeing their chase, he galloped off and vanished past Mount Fangshan.

sentences.zh: 劉惔歎曰：「我入東，正當泊安石渚下耳，不敢復近思曠傍。」

translations.literal: Liu Tan sighed, "When I go east I had better moor below Anshi's islet—I dare not again draw near beside Sikuang."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Tan sighed, "Next time I sail east I shall anchor by Xie An's shoal—I would not moor beside Ruan Yu again."

sentences.zh: 裕雖不博學，論難甚精。

translations.literal: Although Yu was not broadly learned, in disputation he was very acute.
translations.idiomatic: He was no polymath, yet in debate he was razor-keen.

sentences.zh: 嘗問謝萬云：「未見《四本論》，君試為言之。

translations.literal: He once asked Xie Wan, "I have not seen the 'Treatise on the Four Roots'; please try to expound it."
translations.idiomatic: He once asked Xie Wan to summarize the lost "Treatise on the Four Roots."

sentences.zh: 」萬敘說既畢，裕以傅嘏為長，於是構辭數百言，精義入微，聞者皆嗟味之。

translations.literal: When Wan had finished narrating, Yu held Fu Gu right and on that account composed several hundred words whose fine points entered the subtle; listeners all sighed and savored them.
translations.idiomatic: After Xie Wan's précis he sided with Fu Gu's thesis and improvised hundreds of words so subtle the audience savored every line.

sentences.zh: 裕嘗以人不須廣學，正應以禮讓為先故終日靜默，無所修綜，而物自宗焉。

translations.literal: Yu once held that people need not study broadly—that they should instead take yielding ritual as first; therefore all day he was silent and still, practicing nothing, yet things of their own accord took him as their model.
translations.idiomatic: He argued one need not read widely if ritual yielding came first; sitting silent without display, he still became the cynosure of the age.

sentences.zh: 在剡曾有好車，借無不給。

translations.literal: While in Shan he once had a fine carriage and lent it whenever asked without refusing.
translations.idiomatic: In Shan county he owned a fine carriage and lent it freely.

sentences.zh: 有人葬母，意欲借而不敢言。

translations.literal: Someone was burying his mother and wished to borrow but did not dare speak.
translations.idiomatic: A neighbor needed it for his mother's funeral yet dared not ask.

sentences.zh: 後裕聞之，乃歎曰：「吾有車而使人不敢借，何以車為！

translations.literal: Later when Yu heard of it he sighed, "I possess a carriage yet make others afraid to borrow—what use is a carriage!"
translations.idiomatic: Learning this, Ruan Yu cried, "What good is a carriage that frightens borrowers?"

sentences.zh: 」遂命焚之。

translations.literal: He thereupon ordered it burned.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered it burned on the spot.

sentences.zh: 在東山久之，復征散騎常侍，領國子祭酒。

translations.literal: East of the mountain he stayed long; again he was summoned Regular Cavalier Attendant, concurrently libationer of the national academy.
translations.idiomatic: Long settled east of Shan, he was recalled as Regular Cavalier Attendant and libationer of the national university.

sentences.zh: 俄而復以為金紫光祿大夫，領琅邪王師。

translations.literal: Soon again he was made grand master of the palace with golden purple and purple ribbons, concurrently tutor to the Prince of Langye.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was offered golden-purple grand master and tutor to the Prince of Langye.

sentences.zh: 經年敦逼，並無所就。

translations.literal: Year after year they pressed him sternly; he accepted none of the posts.
translations.idiomatic: Year on year the court pressed him; he never took office.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞周閔奏裕及謝安違詔累載，並應有罪，禁錮終身，詔書貰之。

translations.literal: Palace aide in the censorate Zhou Min impeached Yu and Xie An for disobeying edicts many years; both ought to be guilty and barred for life; an edict pardoned them.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Zhou Min charged him and Xie An with years of ignoring summons; the throne forgave them.

sentences.zh: 或問裕曰：「子屢辭徵聘，而宰二郡，何邪？

translations.literal: Someone asked Yu, "You repeatedly decline summons and appointments, yet you governed two commanderies—why?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone asked why he shunned high appointments yet twice ran a commandery.

sentences.zh: 」裕曰：「雖屢辭王命，非敢為高也。

translations.literal: Yu said, "Although I have repeatedly declined royal commands, I do not dare set myself on high.
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "I refuse imperial call not from lofty pride.

sentences.zh: 吾少無宦情，兼拙於人間，既不能躬耕自活，必有所資，故曲躬二郡。

translations.literal: In youth I lacked desire for office, and besides I am clumsy among men; since I could not plow fields to support myself I had to have some resource, therefore I bent body to two commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: I never craved office and am awkward among men; unable to farm for a living, I bent twice to local posts.

sentences.zh: 豈以騁能，私計故耳。

translations.literal: How could that be to display ability—it was private calculation, that is all."
translations.idiomatic: That was survival, not swagger."
