sentences.zh: 」年六十二卒。

translations.literal: He died at sixty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-two.

sentences.zh: 三子：傭、寧、普。

translations.literal: He had three sons: Yong, Ning, and Pu.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Yong, Ning, and Pu.

sentences.zh: 傭，早卒。

translations.literal: Yong died early.
translations.idiomatic: Yong died young.

sentences.zh: 甯，鄱陽太守。

translations.literal: Ning was governor of Poyang.
translations.idiomatic: Ning governed Poyang.

sentences.zh: 普，驃騎諮議參軍。

translations.literal: Pu was adviser in the household to the general of agile cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Pu served as adviser to the general of agile cavalry.

sentences.zh: 傭子歆之，中領軍。

translations.literal: Yong's son was Xinzhi, leader of the central office.
translations.idiomatic: Yong's son Ruan Xinzhi rose to chief of the central guard.

sentences.zh: 甯子腆，秘書監。

translations.literal: Ning's son was Tian, director of the palace library.
translations.idiomatic: Ning's son Ruan Tian became palace librarian.

sentences.zh: 腆弟萬齡及歆之子彌之，元熙中並列顯位。

translations.literal: Tian's younger brother Wanling together with Xinzhi's son Mizhi in the Yuanxi years both rose to prominent position.
translations.idiomatic: Tian's brother Wanling and Xinzhi's son Mizhi both reached high rank under the final Jin emperors.

sentences.zh: 嵇康，字叔夜，譙國銍人也。

translations.literal: Ji Kang, courtesy name Shuye, was a native of Zhi in the kingdom of Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Kang, courtesy name Shuye, came from Zhi in Qiao.

sentences.zh: 其先姓奚，會稽上虞人，以避怨，徙焉。

translations.literal: His ancestors had borne the surname Xi and were men of Shangyu in Kuaiji; to avoid a feud they removed hither.
translations.idiomatic: His clan originally surnamed Xi in Shangyu, Kuaiji, and moved here to escape a blood feud.

sentences.zh: 銍有嵇山，家於其側，因而命氏。

translations.literal: In Zhi there is Ji Mountain; his family dwelled beside it and took the surname from it.
translations.idiomatic: A Ji ridge stood near Zhi; they settled beside it and adopted Ji as their name.

sentences.zh: 兄喜，有當世才，曆太僕、宗正。

translations.literal: His elder brother Xi had talent for the age and served as chamberlain for the mounted escort and chamberlain for the imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Ji Xi was a man of affairs, rising to grand coachman and chamberlain for the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 康早孤，有奇才，遠邁不群。

translations.literal: Kang was orphaned early and had marvelous talent, far surpassing the common run.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, he showed genius that towered over others.

sentences.zh: 身長七尺八寸，美詞氣，有風儀，而土木形骸，不自藻飾，人以為龍章鳳姿，天質自然。

translations.literal: His height was seven chi eight cun; his words and bearing were beautiful, his mien imposing, yet like clay or wood in bodily form he did not adorn himself; people thought him dragon-pattern and phoenix bearing, nature's own purity.
translations.idiomatic: He stood seven chi eight cun, spoke with grace, yet treated his body like unworked clay—no self-adornment—so men saw dragon markings and phoenix mien, utterly natural.

sentences.zh: 恬靜寡欲，含垢匿瑕，寬簡有大量。

translations.literal: He was tranquil and quiet with few desires, concealing flaws and holding grudges within broad tolerance and great capacity.
translations.idiomatic: Calm, wanting little, he swallowed slights and bore insults with large-minded ease.

sentences.zh: 學不師受，博覽無不該通，長好《老》《莊》。

translations.literal: In learning he had no teacher but read widely without failing to master it all; especially he loved Laozi and Zhuangzi.
translations.idiomatic: Untutored yet omnivorous in reading, he cherished Laozi and Zhuangzi above all.

sentences.zh: 與魏宗室婚，拜中散大夫。

translations.literal: By marriage with Wei imperial kin he was appointed grand master of the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Marriage to Wei imperial women won him the title grand master of the palace.

sentences.zh: 常修養性服食之事，彈琴詠詩，自足於懷。

translations.literal: Constantly he cultivated matters of nurturing nature and ingesting elixirs, strumming the zither and chanting poems, self-sufficient in his breast.
translations.idiomatic: He practiced longevity arts, swallowed drugs, played the zither, and chanted poetry—content in his own mind.

sentences.zh: 以為神仙稟之自然，非積學所得，至於導養得理，則安期、彭祖之倫可及，乃著《養生論》。

translations.literal: He held that immortals receive their endowment from nature, not what accumulated study can attain; as to guiding nurture obtaining principle, then the likes of Anqi and Pengzu can be reached, and therefore he composed "On Nurturing Life."
translations.idiomatic: Immortals, he argued, are born, not made; yet proper breath-cultivation could match Anqi or Pengzu—hence his treatise "On Nurturing Life."

sentences.zh: 又以為君子無私，其論曰：「夫稱君子者，心不措乎是非，而行不違乎道者也。

translations.literal: Also he held that the gentleman has no selfishness; his essay says: "So-called 'gentleman' means the heart does not set store by right and wrong, yet conduct does not transgress the Way."
translations.idiomatic: He also taught that the gentleman is selfless: "The gentleman's mind does not clutch at right and wrong, yet his acts never leave the Way."

sentences.zh: 何以言之？

translations.literal: How do we say this?
translations.idiomatic: Why is this so?

sentences.zh: 夫氣靜神虛者，心不存于矜尚；

translations.literal: As for one whose ether is still and spirit empty, the heart does not harbor pride and self-esteem;
translations.idiomatic: When breath is quiet and spirit open, the mind holds no vanity or rivalry;

sentences.zh: 體亮心達者，情不繫於所欲。

translations.literal: As for one whose substance is bright and whose mind comprehends, feeling is not bound by what he desires.
translations.idiomatic: When body and mind are clear, passion no longer clings to craving.

sentences.zh: 矜尚不存乎心，故能越名教而任自然；

translations.literal: Pride and self-esteem are not stored in the heart; therefore one can transcend name-and-teaching and trust what is natural.
translations.idiomatic: With vanity gone from the heart, you step past moral labels and yield to nature.

sentences.zh: 情不繫於所欲，故能審貴賤而通物情。

translations.literal: Because feeling is not bound by what he desires, therefore one can examine noble and base and penetrate the feelings of things.
translations.idiomatic: Unhooked from appetite, you weigh high and low and read the temper of things.

sentences.zh: 物情順通，故大道無違；

translations.literal: When the feelings of things run smooth and penetrate, therefore the great Way is not transgressed.
translations.idiomatic: Once things' truth flows freely, nothing violates the great Way.

sentences.zh: 越名任心，故是非無措也。

translations.literal: Transcending name and trusting the mind, therefore right and wrong have nowhere to lodge.
translations.idiomatic: Drop reputation and follow the heart, and quarrels over right and wrong fall away.

sentences.zh: 是故言君子則以無措為主，以通物為美；

translations.literal: Therefore when one speaks of a gentleman one takes 'having nowhere to lodge' as the master rule and 'penetrating things' as beauty.
translations.idiomatic: So the gentleman keeps no fixed doctrine—only luminous accord with reality.

sentences.zh: 言小人則以匿情為非，以違道為闕。

translations.literal: When one speaks of a petty man one takes 'concealing true feeling' as wrong and 'transgressing the Way' as defect.
translations.idiomatic: The petty man hides his heart and breaks the Way—that is his failing.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 匿情矜吝，小人之至惡；

translations.literal: To conceal one's feeling and cling to miserliness is the petty man's utmost evil.
translations.idiomatic: Hoarding feeling and clutching gain is villainy at its worst.

sentences.zh: 虛心無措，君子之篤行也。

translations.literal: Empty mind and nowhere to lodge is the gentleman's solid conduct.
translations.idiomatic: An open mind with no ulterior motive is the gentleman's steadfast path.

sentences.zh: 是以大道言『及吾無身，吾又何患』。

translations.literal: Therefore the great Way speaks of 'When I have no body, what trouble could I have?'
translations.idiomatic: Hence the classic line: lose the self and trouble ends.

sentences.zh: 無以生為貴者，是賢於貴生也。

translations.literal: One who does not deem mere living noble is worthier than those who prize longevity.
translations.idiomatic: Whoever disdains life for life's own sake ranks above mere survivalists.

sentences.zh: 由斯而言，夫至人之用心，固不存有措矣。

translations.literal: From this to speak, the perfected man's use of mind certainly does not harbor 'having somewhere to lodge.'
translations.idiomatic: Thus the sage's mind never camps on fixed answers.

sentences.zh: 故曰『君子行道，忘其為身』，斯言是矣。

translations.literal: Therefore it is said, 'The gentleman walks the Way and forgets it is his body'—this saying is right.
translations.idiomatic: As the adage runs, the gentleman follows the Way until he forgets his own skin—and it is true.

sentences.zh: 君子之行賢也，不察於有度而後行也；

translations.literal: The gentleman's conduct is worthy, yet he does not investigate whether there is measure and afterward act.
translations.idiomatic: His goodness flows without first checking a yardstick.

sentences.zh: 任心無邪，不議於善而後正也；

translations.literal: Trusting his mind without deviance, he does not deliberate on goodness and afterward correct himself.
translations.idiomatic: He follows an upright heart without staging virtue for display.

sentences.zh: 顯情無措，不論於是而後為也。

translations.literal: His true feeling shows and he has nowhere to lodge; he does not debate 'this is so' and afterward enact it.
translations.idiomatic: With motives clear and no scheming, he never debates correctness before acting.

sentences.zh: 是故傲然忘賢，而賢與度會；

translations.literal: Therefore proudly forget 'worthy' and worthiness joins measure of itself.
translations.idiomatic: Forget you are virtuous, and virtue aligns with order.

sentences.zh: 忽然任心，而心與善遇；

translations.literal: Suddenly trusting the mind, the mind meets goodness of itself.
translations.idiomatic: Surrender to the heart, and goodness aligns unbidden.

sentences.zh: 儻然無措，而事與是俱也。

translations.literal: Carelessly having nowhere to lodge, affairs and 'this is so' come together of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Drift without fixed plans, and right action appears on its own.

sentences.zh: 」其略如此。

translations.literal: The gist was roughly thus.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the thrust of his argument.

sentences.zh: 蓋其胸懷所寄，以高契難期，每思郢質。

translations.literal: As for what his breast lodged—because high communion was hard to await, he always longed for a Ying-quality companion to polish him.
translations.idiomatic: In spirit he pined for rare understanding, forever seeking a listener like the Ying whetstone.

sentences.zh: 所與神交者惟陳留阮籍、河內山濤，豫其流者河內向秀、沛國劉伶、籍兄子咸、琅邪王戎，遂為竹林之遊，世所謂「竹林七賢」也。

translations.literal: Those with whom he shared spirit-communion were only Ruan Ji of Chenliu and Shan Tao of Henei; those who swam in the current were Xiang Xiu of Henei, Liu Ling of Pei, Ruan Xian nephew of Ruan Ji, and Wang Rong of Langye—thereupon they roamed the Bamboo Grove, what the age calls the 'Seven Sages of the Bamboo Grove.'
translations.idiomatic: His soul-friends were Ruan Ji and Shan Tao; Xiang Xiu, Liu Ling, Ruan Xian, and Wang Rong rode the same current—the circle later called the Seven Sages of the Bamboo Grove.

sentences.zh: 戎自言與康居山陽二十年，未嘗見其喜慍之色。

translations.literal: Rong himself said that with Kang they dwelled in Shanyang twenty years and never once saw pleasure or irritation show on his face.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Rong said twenty years beside Ji Kang in Shanyang never showed joy or anger on his face.

sentences.zh: 康嘗采藥遊山澤，會其得意，忽焉忘反。

translations.literal: Kang once gathered herbs roaming hills and marshes, and whenever he met his delight would suddenly forget to return.
translations.idiomatic: Gathering herbs among hills and streams, he would vanish for days when rapture seized him.

sentences.zh: 時有樵蘇者遇之，咸謂神。

translations.literal: At times woodcutters and fuel-gatherers met him and all deemed him a god.
translations.idiomatic: Woodsmen who stumbled upon him mistook him for an immortal.

sentences.zh: 至汲郡山中見孫登，康遂從之遊。

translations.literal: Reaching the mountains of Ji commandery he saw Sun Deng, and Kang thereupon followed him wandering.
translations.idiomatic: In the Ji mountains he met recluse Sun Deng and followed him as a disciple.

sentences.zh: 登沉默自守，無所言說。

translations.literal: Deng was silent and guarded himself, saying nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Deng stayed mute, offering not a word.

sentences.zh: 康臨去，登曰：「君性烈而才雋，其能免乎！

translations.literal: When Kang was about to leave, Deng said, 'Sir, your nature is fierce and your talent outstanding—can you escape harm!'
translations.idiomatic: As Ji Kang turned to go, Sun Deng warned, 'Your temper is fire and your talent blazes—how will you dodge disaster?'

sentences.zh: 」康又遇王烈，共入山，烈嘗得石髓如飴，即自服半，餘半與康，皆凝而為石。

translations.literal: Kang also encountered Wang Lie; together they entered the mountains. Lie once obtained stone marrow sweet as malt sugar, then himself swallowed half; the remaining half he gave to Kang, but both portions congealed into stone.
translations.idiomatic: With Wang Lie he found stone marrow sweet as syrup; each tasted half, yet both halves hardened into stone.

sentences.zh: 又於石室中見一卷素書，遽呼康往取，輙不復見。

translations.literal: Again in a stone chamber he saw a roll of plain silk writing, hastily calling Kang to go fetch it; immediately it was no longer seen.
translations.idiomatic: Another time Wang spied a white silk scroll in a grotto and beckoned Ji Kang—by the time he arrived, the book had vanished.

sentences.zh: 烈乃歎曰：「叔夜志趣非常而輒不遇，命也！

translations.literal: Lie then sighed, 'Shuye's aims go beyond the common yet he never meets his encounter—it is fate!'
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lamented, 'Ji Kang's aspirations outsoar the world, yet fortune never smiles—fate alone decides.'

sentences.zh: 」其神心所感，每遇幽逸如此。

translations.literal: What his numinous mind encountered each time met hidden reclusion thusly.
translations.idiomatic: Again and again his spirit met recluses and portents like these.

sentences.zh: 山濤將去選官，舉康自代。

translations.literal: When Shan Tao was about to leave the office of selection he recommended Kang to replace himself.
translations.idiomatic: When Shan Tao resigned the personnel post, he proposed Ji Kang as successor.

sentences.zh: 康乃與濤書告絕，曰：

translations.literal: Kang thereupon wrote Tao a letter breaking relations, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Ji Kang answered with a celebrated letter severing ties:

sentences.zh: 聞足下欲以吾自代，雖事不行，知足下故不知之也。

translations.literal: I have heard that you intend to replace yourself with me; although the affair did not go through, I know you still do not understand me.
translations.idiomatic: 'Though the appointment never happened, you still fail to understand me.'

sentences.zh: 恐足下羞庖人之獨割，引尸祝以自助，故為足下陳其可不。

translations.literal: I fear you are ashamed of the cook's lone carving, and drag in the corpse-prayer to help yourself, therefore for your sake I set forth how it cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: 'Lest you draft the sacrificial priest to do the butcher's work, I spell out why this cannot be.'

sentences.zh: 老子、莊周，吾之師也，親居賤職；

translations.literal: Laozi and Zhuangzi were my teachers; they personally held low posts.
translations.idiomatic: 'Laozi and Zhuangzi—my masters—willingly kept humble offices.'

sentences.zh: 柳下惠、東方朔，達人也，安乎卑位。

translations.literal: Liuxia Hui and Dongfang Shuo were men who had arrived; they were content in base positions.
translations.idiomatic: 'Liuxia Hui and Dongfang Shuo were realized men content in low rank.'

sentences.zh: 吾豈敢短之哉！

translations.literal: How could I dare belittle them!
translations.idiomatic: 'Would I belittle such men?'

sentences.zh: 又仲尼兼愛，不羞執鞭；

translations.literal: Moreover Zhongni loved all, not shamed to hold the groom's whip;
translations.idiomatic: 'Confucius loved humankind and thought nothing demeaning about holding a driver's whip;'

sentences.zh: 子文無欲卿相，而三為令尹，是乃君子思濟物之意也。

translations.literal: Ziwen did not desire minister or chancellor yet thrice became chief intendant—this indeed is the gentleman's thought of aiding the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: 'Ziwen never craved high office yet thrice served as chief intendant—such is the gentleman's urge to help the world.'

sentences.zh: 所謂達能兼善而不渝，窮則自得而無悶。

translations.literal: So-called 'when expanded able to benefit all without wavering; when pressed able to find contentment in himself without vexation.'
translations.idiomatic: 'Able in success to lift everyone without swerving; in failure to rest content in private peace.'

sentences.zh: 以此觀之，故知堯、舜之居世，許由之巖棲，子房之佐漢，接輿之行歌，其揆一也。

translations.literal: Viewed in this light, one knows that Yao and Shun's dwelling in the world, Xu You's cliff-roosting, Ziliang's aiding Han, and Jieyu's walking songs are measured by the same rule.
translations.idiomatic: 'Seen this way, Yao and Shun on the throne, Xu You on a cliff, Zhang Liang serving Han, and mad Jieyu singing past the ruler all obey one inner measure.'

sentences.zh: 仰瞻數君，可謂能遂其志者也。

translations.literal: Looking up at these several gentlemen, one may say they were able to fulfill their aims.
translations.idiomatic: 'Each honored his chosen path.'

sentences.zh: 故君子百行，殊途同致，循性而動，各附所安。

translations.literal: Therefore the gentleman has a hundred conducts; different roads reach the same goal—following nature in movement, each attaches where he finds peace.
translations.idiomatic: 'So the wise pursue a hundred roads that end one way—each follows his nature to where he rests easy.'

sentences.zh: 故有「處朝廷而不出，入山林而不反」之論。

translations.literal: Therefore there is the thesis 'dwell in court yet do not emerge, enter mountains and forests yet do not return.'
translations.idiomatic: 'Hence the old paradox: stay at court yet never "come forth," retreat to the hills yet never "turn back."'

sentences.zh: 且延陵高子臧之風，長卿慕相如之節，意氣所先，亦不可奪也。

translations.literal: Moreover Yanling admired Prince Zang's lofty style, Zhangqing longed for Xiangru's integrity—what their vital breath first affirms cannot be wrested away.
translations.idiomatic: 'Yanjiling prized Gaozi Zang's austerity; Sima Xiangru emulated Lin Xiangru's spine—what the heart affirms first, no power can rip away.'

sentences.zh: 吾每讀《尚子平、臺孝感傳》，慨然慕之，想其為人。

translations.literal: Whenever I read the biographies of Shang Ziping and Tai Xiaowei I sigh deeply and admire them, imagining what manner of men they were.
translations.idiomatic: 'Whenever I read lives like Shang Ziping and Tai Xiaowei I ache with longing.'

sentences.zh: 加少孤露，母兄驕恣，不涉經學，又讀《老》《莊》，重增其放，故使榮進之心日頹，任逸之情轉篤。

translations.literal: Added to losing my father young, exposed and helpless, mother and elder brother arrogant and self-willed, I did not wade into classical study; again reading Laozi and Zhuangzi redoubled my abandon; therefore the mind that strove for glory daily decayed, while the disposition that trusted carefree ease grew firmer.
translations.idiomatic: 'Orphaned, spoiled by mother and brother without classical drill, steeping instead in Laozi-Zhuangzi, my ambition for rank rotted while love of freedom deepened.'

sentences.zh: 阮嗣宗口不論人過，吾每師之，而未能及。

translations.literal: Ruan Sizong never discussed others' faults in speech—each time I take him as teacher and do not match him.
translations.idiomatic: 'Ruan Ji never gossiped—I try to model him and still fall short.'

sentences.zh: 至性過人，與物無傷，惟飲酒過差耳，至為禮法之士所繩，疾之如仇讎，幸賴大將軍保持之耳。

translations.literal: His utmost nature surpassed others; toward beings he did injury to none—only in drinking he somewhat overstepped, so that men of ritual and law bound him and hated him like foe or thief; fortunately he relied on the Grand General who preserved him.
translations.idiomatic: 'His nature was fierce yet gentle to others—only drinking drew ritualists' hatred, until the Grand General shielded him.'

sentences.zh: 吾以不如嗣宗之資，而有慢弛之闕；

translations.literal: I, lacking Sizong's endowment yet possessing the flaw of arrogance and slackness;
translations.idiomatic: 'I lack his gifts yet carry insolence and slackness;'

sentences.zh: 又不識物情，闇於機宜；

translations.literal: again I do not recognize the feelings of things, am dark about what fits the moment;
translations.idiomatic: 'I misread human tides and mistime every move;'

sentences.zh: 無萬石之慎，而有好盡之累；

translations.literal: I lack the caution of the Wan family of stone, yet carry the liability of liking to speak to the end;
translations.idiomatic: 'I am no paragon of stone-faced caution yet always speak my whole mind;'

sentences.zh: 久與事接，疵釁日興，雖欲無患，其可得乎！

translations.literal: long dealing with affairs, flaws and cracks rise daily—even if wishing to avoid trouble, how could it be obtained!
translations.idiomatic: 'long tangled in office, fault lines widen daily—how could I dodge scandal?'

sentences.zh: 又聞道士遺言，餌术黃精，令人久壽，意甚信之。

translations.literal: Again I have heard Daoist remnants' sayings that ingesting atractylodes and polygonatum makes people long-lived; my intent greatly believes this.
translations.idiomatic: 'Daoist lore promises long life from atractylodes and sealwort—I want to believe it.'

sentences.zh: 遊山澤，觀魚鳥，心甚樂之。

translations.literal: Roaming hills and marshes, observing fish and birds, my heart greatly rejoices in this.
translations.idiomatic: 'I exult in roaming hills, greeting fish and birds—'

sentences.zh: 一行作吏，此事便廢，安能舍其所樂，而從其所懼哉！

translations.literal: Once one row takes up being an official, these affairs are cast aside—how could I abandon what I delight in and follow what I fear!
translations.idiomatic: 'the moment I buckle on an official seal, joy ends—could I trade beloved freedom for feared bondage?'

sentences.zh: 夫人之相知，貴識其天性，因而濟之。

translations.literal: As for men's mutual knowing, what is precious is recognizing their heaven-bestowed nature and thereby aiding them.
translations.idiomatic: 'True friendship reads innate nature and eases it forward:'

sentences.zh: 禹不逼伯成子高，全其長也；

translations.literal: Yu did not force Bozhang Zigao—he completed his loftiness;
translations.idiomatic: 'Yu never forced the sage hermit Bozhang Zigao—honoring his height of character;'

sentences.zh: 仲尼不假蓋于子夏，護其短也。

translations.literal: Zhongni did not borrow an umbrella from Zixia—he protected his shortcoming.
translations.idiomatic: 'Confucius refused Zixia's umbrella—shielding his fussy flaw.'

sentences.zh: 近諸葛孔明不迫元直以入蜀，華子魚不彊幼安以卿相，此可謂能相終始，真相知者也。

translations.literal: Recently Zhuge Liang did not force Xu Shu to enter Shu, Hua Xin did not force You An with minister or chancellor—these can be called able to see one another through from start to finish, truly to know one another.
translations.idiomatic: 'Zhuge Liang never pressed Xu Shu west; Hua Xin never strong-armed Guan You'an into high office—such men knew how to respect a friend's whole arc.'

sentences.zh: 自卜已審，若道盡塗殫則已耳，足下無事冤之令轉於溝壑也。

translations.literal: I have already divined for myself; if the road is exhausted and the track ended, so be it—you have no business wrongly causing me to revolve into ditches and gullies.
translations.idiomatic: 'I have taken my own augury. If my path ends in ruin, so be it—do not push me into the ditch for nothing.'

sentences.zh: 吾新失母兄之歡，意常淒切。

translations.literal: I have newly lost the joy of mother and elder brother; my intent is constantly drenched and cutting.
translations.idiomatic: 'Freshly bereaved of mother and brother, I ache constantly.'

sentences.zh: 女年十三，男年八歲，未及成人，況復多疾，顧此悢悢，如何可言。

translations.literal: My daughter is thirteen sui, my son eight, not yet come to adulthood; moreover they often fall ill—looking at this I am utterly disconsolate; what words can express it.
translations.idiomatic: 'My daughter thirteen, son eight—still children, still sick—how can I bear to leave them?'

sentences.zh: 今但欲守陋巷，教養子孫，時時與親舊敘離闊，陳說平生，濁酒一盃，彈琴一曲，志意畢矣，豈可見黃門而稱貞哉！

translations.literal: Now I only wish to guard a mean lane, instruct sons and grandsons, from time to time with kin and old friends narrate separation and distance, tell plainly a lifetime, one cup of muddy wine, one strum of the zither—with that, intent and will are complete—how could seeing the Yellow Gate count as chastity!
translations.idiomatic: 'I only want a mean lane, music, muddy wine, chatter with old friends, teaching the young—why must I prove chastity to some petty inspector?'

sentences.zh: 若趣欲共登王塗，期於相致，時為懽益，一旦迫之，必發狂疾。

translations.literal: If you hasten to urge us both to climb the king's highway, expecting mutual promotion, at times making merry profit—once you press me I will certainly erupt in madness.
translations.idiomatic: 'If you drag me up the road to power for joint advancement, merriment will sour into frenzy the day you push too hard.'

sentences.zh: 自非重讎，不至此也。

translations.literal: Unless it were deep blood-feud, it would not reach this point.
translations.idiomatic: 'I would not speak so harshly were this not existential.'

sentences.zh: 既以解足下，并以為別。

translations.literal: Having thereby explained to you, I also take this as farewell.
translations.idiomatic: 'Consider this explanation your parting gift.'

sentences.zh: 此書既行，知其不可羈屈也。

translations.literal: Once this letter circulated, they knew he could not be bound or bent.
translations.idiomatic: Once the letter spread, everyone saw he could never be harnessed.

sentences.zh: 性絕巧而好鍛。

translations.literal: By nature he utterly rejected craftiness and loved forging metal.
translations.idiomatic: He loathed petty cleverness and loved to hammer iron.

sentences.zh: 宅中有一柳樹甚茂，乃激水圜之，每夏月，居其下以鍛。

translations.literal: In his house there was one very luxuriant willow tree; he therefore channeled water in a ring around it; each summer month he dwelt beneath it to forge.
translations.idiomatic: A lush willow shaded his yard; he trench-irrigated a ring around it and spent midsummer forging in its cool.

sentences.zh: 東平呂安服康高致，每一相思，輙千里命駕，康友而善之。

translations.literal: Lü An of Dongping admired Kang's lofty aim; whenever he thought of him missingly, always a thousand li he ordered his carriage driven, and Kang befriended him and was good to him.
translations.idiomatic: Lü An of Dongping revered him; a whim of longing sent Lü driving a thousand li, and Ji Kang welcomed him as a dear friend.

sentences.zh: 後安為兄所枉訴，以事繫獄，辭相證引，遂復收康。

translations.literal: Later An was slandered by his elder brother and lodged accusation; because of the affair he was bound in prison, confessions mutually citing each other, thereupon again they seized Kang.
translations.idiomatic: Later Lü An's brother framed him; confessions in jail implicated Ji Kang, who was seized again.

sentences.zh: 康性慎言行，一旦縲紲，乃作《幽憤詩》，曰：

translations.literal: Kang by nature was cautious in speech and conduct; once bound in fetters, he therefore composed 'Poem of Secret Resentment,' saying:
translations.idiomatic: Fastidious in word and deed, he wrote his 'Poem of Secret Resentment' from prison:

sentences.zh: 嗟余薄祜，少遭不造，哀煢靡識，越在襁褓。

translations.literal: Alas, slender was my blessing; in youth I met ill-formation; orphaned and alone I knew nothing, cast still in swaddling clothes.
translations.idiomatic: 'Alas, thin my fate—orphaned young, still swaddled, knowing nothing.'

sentences.zh: 母兄鞠育，有慈無威，恃愛肆好，不訓不師。

translations.literal: Mother and elder brother reared me with kindness but no awe; relying on doting I followed my whims, neither trained nor taught.
translations.idiomatic: 'Mother and brother coddled without discipline; I followed whim, untaught.'

sentences.zh: 爰及冠帶，憑寵自放，抗心希古，任其所尚。

translations.literal: When it came to the capped belt age, trusting favor I let myself go; opposing my mind I longed for antiquity, trusting whatever I admired.
translations.idiomatic: 'At capping I leaned on indulgence, set my heart on antiquity, and chased whatever I admired.'

sentences.zh: 託好《莊》《老》，賤物貴身，志在守樸，養素全真。

translations.literal: Entrusting fondness to Zhuangzi and Laozi, I deemed things base and esteemed the person, my aim set on guarding plainness, nurturing plainness to preserve the whole.
translations.idiomatic: 'Laozi-Zhuangzi taught me to slight things and prize the self—to keep plainness and nurture the whole.'

sentences.zh: 曰予不敏，好善闇人，子玉之敗，屢增惟塵。

translations.literal: They say I am not clever, loving goodness yet dark toward people—Ziyu's defeats repeatedly increased the dust of blame.
translations.idiomatic: 'They call me dim—loving good yet blind to men—like Ziyu's defeats piling blame.'

sentences.zh: 大人含弘，藏垢懷恥。

translations.literal: Great men embrace vastness, hiding grime and cherishing shame.
translations.idiomatic: 'Great souls embrace shame to hide another's stain.'

sentences.zh: 人之多僻，政不由己。

translations.literal: That men are many-sided, government does not come from oneself.
translations.idiomatic: 'Men are crooked; rule never rests with oneself alone.'

sentences.zh: 惟此褊心，顯明臧否；

translations.literal: Only this narrow heart makes manifest what is good and bad;
translations.idiomatic: My narrow heart alone blurts judgments of good and bad.

sentences.zh: 感悟思愆，恒若創痏。

translations.literal: Moved to realization I reflect on faults, constantly as if wounded anew.
translations.idiomatic: 'Awakened, I brood on faults like fresh wounds.'

sentences.zh: 欲寡其過，謗議沸騰，性不傷物，頻致怨憎。

translations.literal: Wishing to reduce my faults, slander and discussion boil over; my nature does not harm things, yet again and again I incur hatred and loathing.
translations.idiomatic: 'I try to curb fault, yet slander boils; I harm no creature, yet hatred gathers.'

sentences.zh: 昔慙柳惠，今愧孫登，內負宿心，外恧良朋。

translations.literal: Formerly I was shamed before Liuxia Hui; now I blush before Sun Deng; inwardly I betray my longstanding intent; outwardly I feel abashed before good friends.
translations.idiomatic: 'Once I blushed before Liuxia Hui; now before Sun Deng—betraying my old vow, shaming true friends.'

sentences.zh: 仰慕嚴、鄭，樂道閑居，與世無營，神氣晏如。

translations.literal: I look up to Yan Junping and Zheng Zizhen, delighting in the Way in idle dwelling; with the world I have no striving; spirit and bearing are tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: 'I revere Yan Zun and Zheng Zizhen, who loved the Way in quiet homes—no striving with the world, spirits calm.'

sentences.zh: 咨予不淑，嬰累多虞。

translations.literal: Alas for my lack of virtue; I have been encircled by many calamities.
translations.idiomatic: 'Alas, weak my virtue—trouble rings me round.'

sentences.zh: 匪降自天，寔由頑疎，理弊患結，卒致囹圄。

translations.literal: Not sent down from Heaven—it truly comes from my stubborn negligence; principle broke and troubles knotted, ending in fetters and prison.
translations.idiomatic: 'Not heaven's curse—my own stubborn slack snapped principle into jail.'

sentences.zh: 對答鄙訊，縶此幽阻，實恥訟冤，時不我與。

translations.literal: Answering base interrogations, tied in this hidden obstruction—truly ashamed to litigate wrong, the time is not with me.
translations.idiomatic: 'Grilled by vile questions, tangled here—ashamed to plead innocence, the hour is wrong.'

sentences.zh: 雖曰義直，神辱志沮，澡身滄浪，曷云能補。

translations.literal: Although they say the meaning is straight, spirit is humiliated and intent is daunted; though I bathe my body in the Canglang waters, how can that make amends!
translations.idiomatic: 'Though my case is just, my spirit is broken; even bathing in Canglang's stream cannot wash the stain.'

sentences.zh: 雍雍鳴雁，厲翼北遊，順時而動，得意忘憂。

translations.literal: Harmoniously crying wild geese, they whet wings and roam north, moving in accord with the season, forgetting care in their contentment.
translations.idiomatic: 'Wild geese cry in tune, beat north on season's cue, carefree in joy.'

sentences.zh: 嗟我憤歎，曾莫能疇。

translations.literal: Alas for my bitter sighs—never able to match them.
translations.idiomatic: 'Alas, my rage—never their match.'

sentences.zh: 事與願違，遘茲淹留，窮達有命，亦又何求？

translations.literal: Affairs oppose my wishes; I meet this dragging stay—poverty and success have fate—what again would I seek?
translations.idiomatic: 'Events thwart my will; I linger here—riches and ruin are fated—what more to seek?'

sentences.zh: 古人有言，善莫近名。

translations.literal: The ancients had a saying: nothing is better than staying near to fame.
translations.idiomatic: 'The ancients said: best stay shy of renown.'

sentences.zh: 奉時恭默，咎悔不生。

translations.literal: Serving the times respectfully silent, fault and regret do not arise.
translations.idiomatic: 'Serve the age in humble silence—no regret rises.'

sentences.zh: 萬石周慎，安親保榮。

translations.literal: The Wan family's stone caution secures kin and preserves glory.
translations.idiomatic: 'The Wan clan's stone-like care kept kin safe and honor bright.'

sentences.zh: 世務紛紜，祗攪余情，安樂必誡，乃終利貞。

translations.literal: Worldly business in confusion only stirs my feeling; peace and joy must be guarded—only then does one end in profitable constancy.
translations.idiomatic: 'Worldly clamor stirs my heart; guard peace and joy to end in lasting good.'

sentences.zh: 煌煌靈芝，一年三秀；

translations.literal: Brightly brilliant numen mushroom, thrice in a year it flowers;
translations.idiomatic: The numinous lingzhi blazes forth three times each year.

sentences.zh: 予獨何為，有志不就。

translations.literal: I alone do what—having aspiration yet not achieving.
translations.idiomatic: So why am I stalled—high aims I never reach?

sentences.zh: 懲難思復，心焉內疚，庶勖將來，無馨無臭。

translations.literal: Chastened by hardship I think of returning; my heart inwardly bears blame; hoping to rouse what is to come—neither fragrance nor stench.
translations.idiomatic: Scarred by disaster I yearn for renewal, gnawed by guilt, vowing the morrow will bear neither fame nor infamy.

sentences.zh: 採薇山阿，散發巖岫，永嘯長吟，頤神養壽。

translations.literal: Gathering fern on the mountain slope, loosening hair in rocky recesses, forever whistling, long chanting, nourishing spirit to lengthen life.
translations.idiomatic: I will pluck ferns in glens, loose my hair on cliffs, whistle for life, and breathe to lengthen years.

sentences.zh: 初，康居貧，嘗與向秀共鍛於大樹之下，以自贍給。

translations.literal: At first Kang dwelled in poverty; he once together with Xiang Xiu forged metal under a great tree to supply himself.
translations.idiomatic: Once, destitute, he hammered iron under a tree with Xiang Xiu to earn his keep.

sentences.zh: 潁川鐘會，貴公子也，精練有才辯，故往造焉。

translations.literal: Zhong Hui of Yingchuan was a noble young lord, refined and talented in disputation; therefore he went to visit him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Hui—a polished aristocrat—paid a call hoping to spar in debate.

sentences.zh: 康不為之禮，而鍛不輟。

translations.literal: Kang did not observe ritual for him but did not stop forging.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Kang ignored him and kept hammering.

sentences.zh: 良久會去，康謂曰：「何所聞而來？

translations.literal: After a long while Hui was about to leave; Kang said to him, "What did you hear that you came?"
translations.idiomatic: As Zhong rose to leave, Ji Kang asked, "What rumor brought you?"

sentences.zh: 何所見而去？

translations.literal: What did you see that you go?
translations.idiomatic: "What sight sends you away?"

sentences.zh: 」會曰：「聞所聞而來，見所見而去。

translations.literal: Hui said, "I heard what I heard and therefore came; I saw what I saw and therefore go."
translations.idiomatic: Zhong snapped, "I came for what I heard; I leave from what I saw."

sentences.zh: 」會以此憾之。

translations.literal: Hui on this account nursed resentment against him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong nursed a grudge.

sentences.zh: 及是，言于文帝曰：「嵇康，臥龍也，不可起。

translations.literal: When it came to this he spoke to Emperor Wen saying, "Ji Kang is a crouching dragon—he cannot be raised."
translations.idiomatic: At his chance he told Sima Zhao, "Ji Kang is a sleeping dragon you will never harness."

sentences.zh: 公無憂天下，顧以康為慮耳。

translations.literal: Your Grace need not worry about All-under-Heaven; only take thought about Kang.
translations.idiomatic: "Forget the realm—worry about Ji Kang."

sentences.zh: 」因譖「康欲助毌丘儉，賴山濤不聽。

translations.literal: Thereupon slandering: "Kang desired to aid Wuqiu Jian, fortunately Shan Tao did not listen."
translations.idiomatic: He added the lie that Ji Kang meant to join Wuqiu Jian's revolt and was blocked only by Shan Tao.

sentences.zh: 昔齊戮華士，魯誅少正卯，誠以害時亂教，故聖賢去之。

translations.literal: In old days Qi executed Hua Shi, Lu executed Shaozheng Mao—truly because they harmed the age and confused teaching, therefore sages worthies removed them.
translations.idiomatic: "Ancient states executed men who broke the moral order—saints pruned such weeds."

sentences.zh: 康、安等言論放蕩，非毀典謨，帝王者所不宜容。

translations.literal: Kang and An and others in speech were reckless and scoffed at canonical models—what emperors and kings ought not tolerate.
translations.idiomatic: "Ji Kang, Lü An, and their circle sneer at the classics—no throne can tolerate them."

sentences.zh: 宜因釁除之，以淳風俗」。

translations.literal: It is fitting to remove them by seizing an occasion, thereby to purify custom."
translations.idiomatic: "Kill them on a pretext to cleanse society."

sentences.zh: 帝既昵聽信會，遂并害之。

translations.literal: The emperor having already favored listening and trusted Hui, thereupon together put them to death.
translations.idiomatic: The regent, ear bent to Zhong Hui, had them executed together.

sentences.zh: 康將刑東市，太學生三千人請以為師，弗許。

translations.literal: When Kang was about to be executed at the eastern market, three thousand students of the Grand Academy begged to take him as teacher; permission was denied.
translations.idiomatic: Three thousand academy scholars begged to study under him at the block; the court refused.

sentences.zh: 康顧視日影，索琴彈之，曰：「昔袁孝尼嘗從吾學《廣陵散》，吾每靳固之，《廣陵散》於今絕矣！

translations.literal: Kang looked at the sun's shadow, asked for a zither and played it, saying: "In old days Yuan Xiaoni once studied 'Guangling Scattering' with me; each time I was stingy and withheld it; 'Guangling Scattering' is from this day ended!"
translations.idiomatic: He studied the sundial, called for his zither, and said, "Yuan Zhun once begged for the Guangling melody—I was too stingy. Today the Guangling tune dies with me."

sentences.zh: 」時年四十。

translations.literal: At the time he was forty sui.
translations.idiomatic: He was forty.

sentences.zh: 海內之士，莫不痛之。

translations.literal: Men of talent within the seas none did not grieve him.
translations.idiomatic: The empire mourned him.

sentences.zh: 帝尋悟而恨焉。

translations.literal: The emperor soon afterward awakened and regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Zhao soon repented—but too late.

sentences.zh: 初，康嘗游乎洛西，暮宿華陽亭，引琴而彈。

translations.literal: At first Kang once roamed west of the Luo; in the evening he lodged at Huayang post station and drew the zither to play.
translations.idiomatic: Long before, west of the Luo, he lodged at Huayang pavilion and played his zither.

sentences.zh: 夜分，忽有客詣之，稱是古人，與康共談音律，辭致清辯，因索琴彈之，而為《廣陵散》，聲調絕倫，遂以授康，仍誓不傳人，亦不言其姓字。

translations.literal: In the middle of the night suddenly a guest visited him, claiming to be an ancient man; together with Kang he discussed musical theory, his diction lucid and discriminating; he thereupon asked for the zither and played it, performing 'Guangling Scattering,' tones and modes peerless; thereupon he handed it to Kang, swore still not to transmit to others, and also did not state his surname or name.
translations.idiomatic: At midnight a stranger calling himself an ancient shared music theory, played the peerless Guangling score, handed it over, swore Ji Kang to secrecy, and vanished nameless.

sentences.zh: 康善談理，又能屬文，其高情遠趣，率然玄遠。

translations.literal: Kang was good at discussing principle and also able to compose prose; his lofty feeling and remote interest were naturally abstruse and far-reaching.
translations.idiomatic: He argued principle and wrote prose with cool distance always veering toward the arcane.

sentences.zh: 撰上古以來高士為之傳贊，欲友其人於千載也。

translations.literal: He composed biographies and eulogies for worthies from high antiquity onward, desiring to befriend those persons across a thousand ages.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote lives of ancient worthies, courting their ghosts as friends.

sentences.zh: 又作《太師箴》，亦足以明帝王之道焉。

translations.literal: He also composed 'Grand Tutor Admonition,' likewise sufficient to clarify the way of emperors and kings.
translations.idiomatic: His Grand Tutor Admonition spells out kingship itself.

sentences.zh: 復作《聲無哀樂論》，甚有條理。

translations.literal: Again he composed 'On Sound's Lack of Sorrow or Joy,' very well ordered.
translations.idiomatic: His essay "Sound Has Neither Joy Nor Sorrow" is tightly reasoned.

sentences.zh: 子紹，別有傳。

translations.literal: His son Shao has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ji Shao has his own chapter.

sentences.zh: 向秀，字子期，河內懷人也。

translations.literal: Xiang Xiu, courtesy name Ziqi, was a native of Huai in Henei.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Xiu, courtesy Ziqi, came from Huai in Henei.

sentences.zh: 清悟有遠識，少為山濤所知，雅好老莊之學。

translations.literal: He was clear in apprehension and had far-reaching insight; in youth he was known to Shan Tao, and he honored and loved the learning of Laozi and Zhuangzi.
translations.idiomatic: Bright and farsighted, he came early to Shan Tao's notice and loved Daoist texts.

sentences.zh: 莊周著內外數十篇，曆世才士雖有觀者，莫適論其旨統也，秀乃為之隱解，發明奇趣，振起玄風，讀之者超然心悟，莫不自足一時也。

translations.literal: Zhuang Zhou wrote inner and outer chapters numbering several tens; through generations of talented scholars although there were viewers, none hit upon discussing the overall aim; Xiu thereupon wrote a concealed explication for them, elucidating marvellous interests and raising up the dark wind; readers transcended in heart and awakened, none not self-satisfied for a time.
translations.idiomatic: Generations had read Zhuangzi without cracking its spine; Xiang Xiu's commentary awakened readers to a new metaphysical breeze.

sentences.zh: 惠帝之世，郭象又述而廣之，儒墨之跡見鄙，道家之言遂盛焉。

translations.literal: In Emperor Hui's reign Guo Xiang again continued and expanded it; traces of Ru and Mo were despised, and Daoist discourse thereupon flourished.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Xiang later elaborated the same line, burying Confucianism and Mohism under rising Daoist fashion.

sentences.zh: 始，秀欲注，嵇康曰：「此書詎復須注，正是妨人作樂耳。

translations.literal: At first Xiu desired to write commentary; Ji Kang said, "This book—does it again need commentary? It only hinders people from having fun."
translations.idiomatic: When Xiang Xiu began annotating Zhuangzi, Ji Kang joked, "Does that text need glosses? You only spoil the sport."

sentences.zh: 」及成，示康曰：「殊復勝不？

translations.literal: When it was finished he showed Kang saying, "Is it not again superior?"
translations.idiomatic: When the draft was done he asked, "Still not better than the original?"

sentences.zh: 」又與康論養生，辭難往復，蓋欲發康高致也。

translations.literal: Again with Kang he discussed nurturing life, arguments and rebuttals going back and forth—generally intending to draw out Kang's lofty reach.
translations.idiomatic: They sparred over longevity lore simply to draw out Ji Kang's wit.

sentences.zh: 康善鍛，秀為之佐，相對欣然，傍若無人。

translations.literal: Kang was good at forging; Xiu assisted him; facing each other they were glad as if no other people stood beside them.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Kang smithied while Xiang Xiu pumped the bellows, both grinning as if alone in the world.

sentences.zh: 又共呂安灌園于山陽。

translations.literal: Again together with Lü An they watered gardens in Shanyang.
translations.idiomatic: With Lü An he tended gardens in Shanyang.

sentences.zh: 康既被誅，秀應本郡計入洛。

translations.literal: After Kang was executed, Xiu answered the commandery's accounting and entered Luo.
translations.idiomatic: After the execution Xiang Xiu answered a census call and went to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 文帝問曰：「聞有箕山之志，何以在此？

translations.literal: Emperor Wen asked, "I have heard you had the mind of Mount Ji—why are you here?"
translations.idiomatic: Sima Zhao asked why a Mount-Ji recluse had come to court.

sentences.zh: 」秀曰：「以為巢許狷介之士，未達堯心，豈足多慕。

translations.literal: Xiu said, "I supposed the recluses Chao and Xu were narrow men of fastidious mind who did not comprehend Yao's intent—how could they be worth much admiration?"
translations.idiomatic: He replied that hermits like Chao and Xu were cramped pedants who never grasped Yao's mind—not worth imitating.

sentences.zh: 」帝甚悅。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The regent beamed.

sentences.zh: 秀乃自此役，作《思舊賦》云：

translations.literal: Xiu thereupon from this service composed 'Rhapsody on Thinking of the Old,' saying:
translations.idiomatic: Then he wrote his "Rhapsody Recalling Old Friends":

sentences.zh: 余與嵇康、呂安居止接近，其人並有不羈之才，嵇意遠而疏，呂心曠而放，其後並以事見法。

translations.literal: Xiu with Ji Kang and Lü An dwelled close; those men together possessed unrestrained talent—Ji's intent was far-off and aloof, Lü's mind was broad and unrestrained; afterward both because of affairs met the law.
translations.idiomatic: "Ji Kang kept a cool distance, Lü An was effusive; both died by the law."

sentences.zh: 嵇博綜伎藝，於絲竹特妙，臨當就命，顧視日影，索琴而彈之。

translations.literal: Ji comprehensively mastered crafts and arts; in silk and bamboo he was especially marvelous; when about to accept the command he looked at the sun's shadow, asked for the zither and played it.
translations.idiomatic: "Ji Kang mastered every art; facing execution he read the sundial and played his zither one last time."

sentences.zh: 逝將西邁，經其舊廬。

translations.literal: About to travel west, I pass their old huts.
translations.idiomatic: "Now I ride west past their lanes."

sentences.zh: 于時日薄虞泉，寒冰淒然。

translations.literal: At that time the sun neared Yu-quan; icy cold was bleak.
translations.idiomatic: "The sun sank toward Yuquan; ice-bit air bit sharp."

sentences.zh: 鄰人有吹笛者，發聲寥亮。

translations.literal: A neighbor had someone blowing the flute; the sound issued clear and bright.
translations.idiomatic: "A neighbor's flute pierced the dusk, bright and clear."

sentences.zh: 追想曩昔遊宴之好，感音而歎，故作賦曰：

translations.literal: Pursuing thought of former days' roaming and feasting pleasures, moved by the sound I sighed; therefore I compose the rhapsody saying:
translations.idiomatic: "Moved by that sound, I sigh for old feasts and set brush to silk:"

sentences.zh: 將命適於遠京兮，遂旋反以北徂。

translations.literal: About to set off for the distant capital, then wheeling back to go north.
translations.idiomatic: "Ordered to the distant capital, I wheel my carriage north again;"

sentences.zh: 濟黃河以泛舟兮，經山陽之舊居。

translations.literal: Crossing the Yellow River by drifting boat, passing the old dwellings at Shanyang.
translations.idiomatic: "I float the Yellow River and pass our Shanyang homes;"

sentences.zh: 瞻曠野之蕭條兮，息餘駕乎城隅。

translations.literal: Gazing on the desolation of the open wilds, I rest my team at the city's corner.
translations.idiomatic: "I scan bleak fields and halt my horses at the wall;"

sentences.zh: 踐二子之遺跡兮，曆窮巷之空廬。

translations.literal: Treading the two gentlemen's remaining traces, I traverse the empty huts of the poor lane.
translations.idiomatic: "I walk their lanes—only empty cottages;"

sentences.zh: 歎《黍離》之湣周兮，悲《麥秀》於殷墟。

translations.literal: I sigh at 'Millet's Ripples' pitying Zhou; I grieve at 'Ripening Wheat' on Yin ruins.
translations.idiomatic: "I sigh like the Odes for fallen Zhou, grieve like the wheat song for lost Yin;"

sentences.zh: 惟追昔以懷今兮，心徘徊以躊躇。

translations.literal: Only pursuing the past I embrace the present; my heart paces and hesitates.
translations.idiomatic: "Past and present knot my heart in hesitation;"

sentences.zh: 棟宇在而弗毀兮，形神逝其焉如。

translations.literal: The rafters stand yet are not destroyed; where have form and spirit gone?
translations.idiomatic: "The beams still stand—where are their souls?"

sentences.zh: 昔李斯之受罪兮，歎黃犬而長吟。

translations.literal: In old days Li Si when receiving punishment sighed for the yellow dog and chanted long.
translations.idiomatic: "Li Si, condemned, moaned for his yellow hound;"

sentences.zh: 悼嵇生之永辭兮，顧日影而彈琴。

translations.literal: I mourn Lord Ji's forever parting, looking at the sun's shadow and strumming the zither.
translations.idiomatic: "I mourn Ji Kang, who read the shadow and played his zither;"

sentences.zh: 托運遇于領會兮，寄余命於寸陰。

translations.literal: Entrusting fortune's meeting to a moment's grasp, I lodge my remaining life in an inch of shade.
translations.idiomatic: "I lodge my fate in a breath of shadow;"

sentences.zh: 聽鳴笛之慷慨兮，妙聲絕而復尋。

translations.literal: Listening to the flute's stirring sound, the marvellous tones end yet I seek them again.
translations.idiomatic: "The flute's passion fades yet I strain to hear;"

sentences.zh: 佇駕言其將邁兮，故援翰以寫心。

translations.literal: Standing, my carriage about to set off, therefore I take brush to write the heart.
translations.idiomatic: "My chariot waits—so I dip ink to bare the heart."

sentences.zh: 後為散騎侍郎，轉黃門侍郎、散騎常侍，在朝不任職，容跡而已。

translations.literal: Later he served as Gentleman of the Palace Gate, was transferred to Gentleman in the Yellow Gate and Regular Cavalier Attendant; at court he did not take up duties but only kept a footprint.
translations.idiomatic: Later he held titular court posts, leaving no mark of power.

sentences.zh: 卒於位。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 二子：純、悌。

translations.literal: He had two sons: Chun and Ti.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Xiang Chun and Xiang Ti.

sentences.zh: 劉伶，字伯倫，沛國人也。

translations.literal: Liu Ling, courtesy name Bolun, was a native of the kingdom of Pei.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ling, courtesy Bolun, came from Pei.

sentences.zh: 身長六尺，容貌甚陋。

translations.literal: His height was six chi; his appearance was very homely.
translations.idiomatic: He stood six chi tall and was famously ugly.

sentences.zh: 放情肆志，常以細宇宙齊萬物為心。

translations.literal: He let feeling run free and indulged his intent, constantly taking as his mind to treat the cosmos as tiny and the myriad things as equal.
translations.idiomatic: He treated heaven and earth as a speck and the myriad things as equals.

sentences.zh: 澹默少言，不妄交遊，與阮籍、嵇康相遇，欣然神解，攜手入林。

translations.literal: He was placid and silent, spoke little, did not rashly make social rounds; encountering Ruan Ji and Ji Kang he was glad as if spirit had understood, and hand in hand they entered the grove.
translations.idiomatic: Silent and solitary until he met Ruan Ji and Ji Kang—then he plunged into the grove with them, soul alight.

sentences.zh: 初不以家產有無介意。

translations.literal: At first he did not take notice whether his household had property or not.
translations.idiomatic: Wealth never crossed his mind.

sentences.zh: 常乘鹿車，攜一壺酒，使人荷鍤而隨之，謂曰：「死便埋我。

translations.literal: He constantly rode a deer cart, carried one pot of wine, had a man follow bearing a shovel on his shoulder, saying to him, "When I die, bury me."
translations.idiomatic: He rode a deer cart with wine while a servant trailed with a spade, saying, "Where I drop, dig me in."

sentences.zh: 」其遺形骸如此。

translations.literal: Such was his casting off body form.
translations.idiomatic: So little did he cling to the flesh.

sentences.zh: 嘗渴甚，求酒于其妻。

translations.literal: Once he was very thirsty and sought wine from his wife.
translations.idiomatic: Once parched, he begged wine from his wife.

sentences.zh: 妻捐酒毀器，涕泣諫曰：「君酒太過，非攝生之道，必宜斷之。

translations.literal: His wife threw away the wine and smashed the vessels, weeping as she remonstrated, saying, "Sir, your drinking is too excessive; it is not the way to nurture life—you must break it off."
translations.idiomatic: She smashed the jars and wept, "Your drinking will kill you—you must quit."

sentences.zh: 」伶曰：「善！

translations.literal: Ling said, "Good!"
translations.idiomatic: He said, "Well spoken!"

sentences.zh: 吾不能自禁，惟當祝鬼神自誓耳。

translations.literal: I cannot restrain myself; only when I pray to ghosts and spirits to swear myself.
translations.idiomatic: "I cannot stop alone—I must swear off drink before the spirits."

sentences.zh: 便可具酒肉。

translations.literal: You may prepare wine and meat."
translations.idiomatic: "Set out wine and meat for the oath."

sentences.zh: 」妻從之。

translations.literal: His wife followed this.
translations.idiomatic: She obeyed.

sentences.zh: 伶跪祝曰：「天生劉伶，以酒為名。

translations.literal: Ling knelt in prayer saying, "Heaven gave birth to Liu Ling, using wine as his name.
translations.idiomatic: He knelt and intoned, "Heaven spawned Liu Ling to prove the power of wine.

sentences.zh: 一飲一斛，五斗解酲。

translations.literal: One drink a hu, five dou dispels hangover.
translations.idiomatic: "One hu steadies me; five dou clears the dregs."

sentences.zh: 婦兒之言，慎不可聽。

translations.literal: Wives' and children's words must by no means be heeded."
translations.idiomatic: "Never heed a wife or child."

sentences.zh: 」仍引酒禦肉，隗然復醉。

translations.literal: Thereupon he drew wine and ate meat, and sank drunk again.
translations.idiomatic: Then he ate, drank, and passed out again.

sentences.zh: 嘗醉與俗人相忤，其人攘袂奮拳而往。

translations.literal: Once drunk he crossed a vulgar man who resented him; that man rolled sleeves and shook fists as he advanced.
translations.idiomatic: Drunk once, he insulted a bully who came swinging fists.

sentences.zh: 伶徐曰：「雞肋不足以安尊拳。

translations.literal: Ling slowly said, "Chicken ribs are not enough to settle your honored fists."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ling drawled, "These ribs of a frame cannot hold your mighty fists."

sentences.zh: 」其人笑而止。

translations.literal: That man laughed and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The man laughed and walked off.

sentences.zh: 伶雖陶兀昏放，而機應不差。

translations.literal: Although Ling was muddled in pottery and benighted in abandon, his responses to circumstance missed nothing.
translations.idiomatic: For all his stupor his timing was exact.

sentences.zh: 未嘗厝意文翰，惟著《酒德頌》一篇。

translations.literal: He never set intent on literary brush; only he composed one piece, 'Eulogy on the Virtue of Wine.'
translations.idiomatic: He wrote almost nothing save the "Eulogy on the Virtue of Wine."

sentences.zh: 其辭曰：

translations.literal: Its wording says:
translations.idiomatic: It begins:

sentences.zh: 有大人先生，以天地為一朝，萬期為須臾，日月為扃牖，八荒為庭衢。

translations.literal: There was a great man, master, who treated heaven and earth as one dawn, myriad epochs as a moment, sun and moon as door and window, the eight wilds as courtyard and avenue.
translations.idiomatic: "A great soul treats the cosmos as one morning, eternity as a blink, sun and moon as windows, the eight wastes as his courtyard."

sentences.zh: 行無轍跡，居無室廬，幕天席地，縱意所如。

translations.literal: In going he left no rut-traces; in dwelling he had no chamber or hut; he used heaven as curtain and earth as mat, following his intent wherever it went.
translations.idiomatic: "He leaves no tracks, owns no roof—sky his curtain, earth his mat—roaming wherever whim leads."

sentences.zh: 止則操卮執觚，動則挈榼提壺，惟酒是務，焉知其餘。

translations.literal: Stopped, then he grasped goblet and held drinking horn; moving, then he lifted wine-jar and carried pot—only wine was his business; how could he know the rest?
translations.idiomatic: "Stopped, he grips cup and horn; moving, he hoists keg and jug—wine is his trade; the rest is noise."

sentences.zh: 有貴介公子、搢紳處士，聞吾風聲，議其所以，乃奮袂攘襟，怒目切齒，陳說禮法，是非蜂起。

translations.literal: There were noble young lords and gentry recluses who heard my breeze and reputation, deliberated its causes, then rolled sleeves and clutched lapels, glared with angry eyes and gnashed teeth, rehearsing ritual and law, right and wrong swarming up.
translations.idiomatic: "Pedants hear of him, roll up sleeves, gnash teeth, thundering ritual until right and wrong swarm."

sentences.zh: 先生於是方捧甕承槽，銜杯漱醪，奮髯箕踞，枕曲藉糟，無思無慮，其樂陶陶。

translations.literal: The master thereupon just cradled the jar to catch lees, held cup in mouth rinsing thick brew, whisked beard and sat legs sprawled, pillowed on yeast and leaned on dregs—without thought without care, his joy was exalted.
translations.idiomatic: "The master hugs the vat, rinses mash in his teeth, sprawls on lees—thoughtless, ecstatic."

sentences.zh: 兀然而醉，怳爾而醒。

translations.literal: He was lofty and drunk, suddenly awake.
translations.idiomatic: "He floats drunk, then snaps awake;"

sentences.zh: 靜聽不聞雷霆之聲，熟視不睹泰山之形。

translations.literal: Still listening he did not hear thunder's sound; closely looking he did not see Mount Tai's form.
translations.idiomatic: "Deaf to thunder, blind to Tai;"

sentences.zh: 不覺寒暑之切肌，利欲之感情。

translations.literal: He did not feel cold and heat cutting the flesh, profit and desire touching the feeling.
translations.idiomatic: "numb to frost and flame, deaf to greed;"

sentences.zh: 俯觀萬物，擾擾焉若江海之載浮萍。

translations.literal: Looking down on the myriad things, they teemed as if the rivers and seas carried duckweed.
translations.idiomatic: "Below him creation teems like duckweed on a sea;"

sentences.zh: 二豪侍側焉，如蜾蠃之與螟蛉。

translations.literal: The two heroes standing beside him were as the wasp to the caterpillar.
translations.idiomatic: "the moralists at his side look like wasps beside worms."

sentences.zh: 嘗為建威參軍。

translations.literal: He once served as adjutant to the general who displays might.
translations.idiomatic: He once served as adjutant to the general who displays might.

sentences.zh: 泰始初對策，盛言無為之化。

translations.literal: In Taishi's beginning he answered policy questions, greatly expounding the transformation of non-action.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Taishi he aced the policy exam praising non-action.

sentences.zh: 時輩皆以高第得調，伶獨以無用罷。

translations.literal: His contemporaries all by high rank obtained selection; Ling alone because useless was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Classmates won high placement; Liu Ling alone failed as useless.

sentences.zh: 竟以壽終。

translations.literal: In the end he died at his natural span.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ling died in bed of old age.

sentences.zh: 謝鯤，字幼輿，陳國陽夏人也。

translations.literal: Xie Kun, courtesy name Youyu, was a native of Yangxia in the state of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Kun, courtesy Youyu, came from Yangxia in Chen.

sentences.zh: 祖纘，典農中郎將。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zuan was Colonel of Agriculture in the Garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Xie Zuan commanded the agricultural colonies.

sentences.zh: 父衡，以儒素顯，仕至國子祭酒。

translations.literal: His father Heng was prominent for Confucian plainness and rose to libationer of the national academy.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xie Heng was a noted Confucian scholar who became libationer of the national university.

sentences.zh: 鯤少知名，通簡有高識，不修威儀，好《老》《易》，能歌，善鼓琴，王衍、嵇紹並奇之。

translations.literal: Kun in youth was renowned, comprehending plainness and possessing lofty insight; he did not cultivate awe-inspiring deportment, loved Laozi and the Changes, could sing, was skilled at strumming the zither; Wang Yan and Ji Shao both thought him extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Young Xie Kun was famous for insight and ease—he loved the Changes and Laozi, sang and played zither, and won Wang Yan's and Ji Shao's admiration.

sentences.zh: 永興中，長沙王乂入輔政，時有疾鯤者，言其將出奔。

translations.literal: In the Yongxing era the Prince of Changsha Wang Yi entered to assist government; at the time there was one who resented Kun and said he was about to flee.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yongxing, Prince Wang Yi of Changsha entered the capital; a slanderer claimed Xie Kun meant to desert.

sentences.zh: 乂欲鞭之，鯤解衣就罰，曾無忤容。

translations.literal: Yi wished to flog him; Kun removed his robe and submitted to punishment, never showing a contrary look.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yi ordered a flogging; Xie Kun stripped without flinching.

sentences.zh: 既舍之，又無喜色。

translations.literal: After he was released he also showed no joyful look.
translations.idiomatic: Freed, he showed no elation either.

sentences.zh: 太傅東海王越聞其名，辟為掾，任達不拘，尋坐家僮取官稿除名。

translations.literal: The Grand Tutor Prince of the East Sea Sima Yue heard his name and summoned him as clerk; he was broad-minded and unrestrained, soon sitting because a household slave took official firewood and was stricken from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yue summoned him as clerk; he lost his post when a servant stole official fuel.

sentences.zh: 于時名士王玄、阮修之徒，並以鯤初登宰府，便至黜辱，為之歎恨。

translations.literal: At the time famed scholars such as Wang Xuan and Ruan Xiu, because Kun had just ascended the minister's bureau and then met dismissal and shame, for him sighed in regret.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xuan and Ruan Xiu mourned his fall from the ministry.

sentences.zh: 鯤聞之，方清歌鼓琴，不以屑意，莫不服其遠暢，而恬於榮辱。

translations.literal: When Kun heard of it, he was just singing clearly and strumming the zither, not taking it as worth a speck; none failed to admire his far-reaching openness and his tranquillity toward glory and disgrace.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Kun merely sang and played, unruffled—everyone marveled at his distance from fame.

sentences.zh: 鄰家高氏女有美色，鯤嘗挑之，女投梭，折其兩齒。

translations.literal: The neighbor girl of the Gao clan had beautiful looks; Kun once flirted with her; the girl threw the shuttle, breaking two of his teeth.
translations.idiomatic: He flirted with a neighbor's beauty; she hurled her shuttle and knocked out two teeth.

sentences.zh: 時人為之語曰：「任達不已，幼輿折齒。

translations.literal: People of the time made a saying for him: "Unrestrained to the end, Youyu's teeth are broken."
translations.idiomatic: Wits sang, "So free he lost his teeth—our Youyu!"

sentences.zh: 」鯤聞之，敖然長嘯曰：「猶不廢我嘯歌。

translations.literal: When Kun heard it, he gave a proud long whistle and said, "It still does not stop me from whistling and singing."
translations.idiomatic: He roared with laughter, "She never silenced my song!"

sentences.zh: 」越尋更辟之，轉參軍事。

translations.literal: Yue soon again summoned him and transferred him to adjutant on military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yue soon recalled him as military adjutant.

sentences.zh: 鯤以時方多故，乃謝病去職，避地于豫章。

translations.literal: Kun because the times had many troubles thereupon resigned citing illness, left office, and took refuge in Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Troubled times drove him to resign and flee to Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 嘗行經空亭中夜宿，此亭舊每殺人。

translations.literal: Once traveling he lodged at midnight in an empty pavilion; this pavilion in the past always killed people.
translations.idiomatic: He once slept in a murder-haunted post-house.

sentences.zh: 將曉，有黃衣人呼鯤字令開戶，鯤憺然無懼色，便於窗中度手牽之，胛斷，視之，鹿也，尋血獲焉。

translations.literal: Near dawn a man in yellow called Kun's name ordering him to open the door; Kun was calm without fear, then from the window passed his hand to pull him—the shoulder blade broke; looking at it, it was a deer; following the blood they caught it.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn a yellow-clad voice demanded entry; he reached through the lattice, tore off a shoulder—it was a bleeding deer, not a ghost.

sentences.zh: 爾後此亭無復妖怪。

translations.literal: After that this pavilion never again had uncanny beings.
translations.idiomatic: The haunt never troubled travelers again.

sentences.zh: 左將軍王敦引為長史，以討杜弢功封咸亭侯。

translations.literal: General of the Left Wang Dun appointed him chief clerk; for merit in attacking Du Tao he was enfeoffed marquis of Xianting.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun made him chief clerk; he earned the Xianting marquisate crushing Du Tao.

sentences.zh: 母憂去職，服闋，遷敦大將軍長史。

translations.literal: He left office for mother's mourning; when mourning ended he was promoted to Dun's grand general chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning his mother he became Wang Dun's chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 時王澄在敦坐，見鯤談話無勌，惟歎謝長史可與言，都不眄敦，其為人所慕如此。

translations.literal: At the time Wang Cheng was in Dun's seat; seeing Kun converse tirelessly he only sighed that chief clerk Xie was someone one could talk with, never glancing at Dun—such was the degree others admired him.
translations.idiomatic: At Wang Dun's banquet he talked only to Xie Kun, ignoring Wang Dun—such was his charisma.

sentences.zh: 鯤不徇功名，無砥礪行，居身於可否之間，雖自處若穢，而動不累高。

translations.literal: Kun did not pursue merit and fame, had no grinding conduct, placed himself between yes and no; although in self-placement he seemed base, in movement he did not drag down the high.
translations.idiomatic: He chased neither fame nor polish, lived in moral gray zones, yet never debased the ideal.

sentences.zh: 敦有不臣之跡，顯於朝野。

translations.literal: Dun had traces of a subject's breach of loyalty, manifest at court and in the wilds.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun's treason showed plain to all.

sentences.zh: 鯤知不可以道匡弼，乃優遊寄遇，不屑政事，從容諷議，卒歲而已。

translations.literal: Kun knew he could not be corrected by the Way; thereupon he wandered at ease and lodged his encounters, disdained government affairs, mildly remonstrated and discussed, ending the year thus.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing he could not steer Wang Dun, he drifted, shirked duties, and offered only oblique counsel.

sentences.zh: 每與畢卓、王尼、阮放、羊曼、桓彝、阮孚等縱酒，敦以其名高，雅相賓禮。

translations.literal: Often with Bi Zhuo, Wang Ni, Ruan Fang, Yang Man, Huan Yi, Ruan Fu and others he drank wildly; Dun because his name was high treated him with refined courtesy as guest.
translations.idiomatic: He caroused with the Seven Sages set; Wang Dun honored his name.

sentences.zh: 嘗使至都，明帝在東宮見之，甚相親重。

translations.literal: Once sent to the capital, Emperor Ming while heir apparent saw him and was very intimate and respectful.
translations.idiomatic: Crown prince Sima Shao adored him on a mission to the capital.

sentences.zh: 問曰：「論者以君方庾亮，自謂何如？

translations.literal: He asked, "Critics compare you to Yu Liang—what do you yourself think?"
translations.idiomatic: The heir asked how he compared to Yu Liang.

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「端委廟堂，使百僚準則，鯤不如亮。

translations.literal: He answered, "In cap and robe in the temple hall, making the hundred officials take him as model, Kun is not equal to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "In court regalia, making ministers take their cue, I fall short of Yu Liang.

sentences.zh: 一丘一壑，自謂過之。

translations.literal: For hillock and ravine, I claim to surpass him."
translations.idiomatic: Among hills and streams I surpass him."

sentences.zh: 」溫嶠嘗謂鯤子尚曰：「尊大君豈惟識量淹遠，至於神鑒沈深，雖諸葛瑾之喻孫權不過也。」

translations.literal: Wen Jiao once said to Kun's son Shang, "Your honored father is not only broad in insight and measure—his spiritual mirror is deep; even Zhuge Jin's comparison to Sun Quan does not surpass it."
translations.idiomatic: Wen Jiao told Xie Shang his father's discernment rivaled Zhuge Jin's praise of Sun Quan.

sentences.zh: 及敦將為逆，謂鯤曰：「劉隗奸邪，將危社稷。

translations.literal: When Dun was about to rebel he said to Kun, "Liu Wei is treacherous and evil and will endanger the altars of soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: As Wang Dun plotted revolt he said, "Liu Wei threatens the state.

sentences.zh: 吾欲除君側之惡，匡主濟時，何如？

translations.literal: I desire to remove the evil beside the ruler, rescue the sovereign and aid the times—what of it?"
translations.idiomatic: I will purge the villain beside the throne—what say you?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「隗誠始禍，然城狐社鼠也。

translations.literal: He answered, "Wei indeed begins the calamity, yet he is the fox on the wall and rat at the earth altar."
translations.idiomatic: Xie Kun answered, "Liu Wei is a pest, yet only a fox on the city wall, a rat in the shrine—"

sentences.zh: 」敦怒曰：「君庸才，豈達大理。

translations.literal: Dun angrily said, "Sir is a mediocre talent—how could you comprehend great principle!"
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun snarled that he was a mediocrity.

sentences.zh: 」出鯤為豫章太守，又留不遣，藉其才望，逼與俱下。

translations.literal: He sent Kun out as governor of Yuzhang, again detained him and would not dispatch him, relying on his talent and reputation, forcing him to go downriver together.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun named him governor of Yuzhang yet held him hostage for his prestige.

sentences.zh: 敦至石頭，歎曰：「吾不復得為盛德事矣。

translations.literal: When Dun reached Stone Citadel he sighed, "I shall not again be able to do deeds of abundant virtue."
translations.idiomatic: At Stone Citadel Wang Dun sighed he could no longer play the benefactor.

sentences.zh: 」鯤曰：「何為其然？

translations.literal: Kun said, "Why must it be so?
translations.idiomatic: Xie Kun asked why despair.

sentences.zh: 但使自今以往，日忘日去耳。

translations.literal: Only make it that from now on day by day you forget day by day going."
translations.idiomatic: "From today forget yesterday's grudges, day by day."

sentences.zh: 」初，敦謂鯤曰：「吾當以周伯仁為尚書令，戴若思為僕射。

translations.literal: At first Dun said to Kun, "I shall make Zhou Borén minister of education, Dai Ruosi minister of the left."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun once planned to name Zhou Yi and Dai Yuan to high office.

sentences.zh: 」及至都，復曰：「近來人情何如？

translations.literal: When he reached the capital he again said, "Recently how are people's feelings?"
translations.idiomatic: Entering the capital he asked the mood of the city.

sentences.zh: 」鯤對曰：「明公之舉，雖欲大存社稷，然悠悠之言，實未達高義。

translations.literal: Kun answered, "Your action, although intending greatly to preserve the altars, yet floating rumor in truth has not reached your lofty meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Kun said, "Your move may save the dynasty, but rumor has not caught your noble aim.

sentences.zh: 周顗、戴若思，南北人士之望，明公舉而用之，群情帖然矣。

translations.literal: Zhou Yi and Dai Ruosi are the hope of north and south gentlemen; if Your Excellency raises and employs them, crowd feeling will be calm."
translations.idiomatic: Win the people by elevating Zhou Yi and Dai Yuan."

sentences.zh: 」是日，敦遣兵收周、戴，而鯤弗知，敦怒曰：「君粗疏邪！

translations.literal: That day Dun sent troops to seize Zhou and Dai, while Kun did not know; Dun angrily said, "Are you coarse and careless!
translations.idiomatic: That day Wang Dun arrested Zhou and Dai without telling Xie Kun, then accused him of stupidity.

sentences.zh: 二子不相當，吾已收之矣。

translations.literal: The two men did not suit me; I have already seized them."
translations.idiomatic: "They would not serve me—I have seized them."

sentences.zh: 」鯤與顗素相親重，聞之愕然，若喪諸己。

translations.literal: Kun with Yi had always been intimate and respectful; hearing it he was stunned as if he himself had died.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Kun reeled as if he had died with Zhou Yi.

sentences.zh: 參軍王驕以敦誅顗，諫之甚切，敦大怒，命斬嶠，時人士畏懼，莫敢言者。

translations.literal: Adjutant Wang Jiao because Dun executed Yi remonstrated very cuttingly; Dun was greatly angry and ordered Jiao beheaded; at the time men of standing were afraid and none dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jiao protested Zhou Yi's death; Wang Dun ordered him executed—none dared speak.

sentences.zh: 鯤曰：「明公舉大事，不戮一人。

translations.literal: Kun said, "Your Excellency raises a great affair yet does not kill a single man.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Kun said, "You launch a coup yet kill no one—"

sentences.zh: 嶠以獻替忤旨，便以釁鼓，不亦過乎！

translations.literal: Yet Jiao because loyal remonstrance offended your intent would be executed and smeared on the signal-drum—is that not excessive!"
translations.idiomatic: yet for one blunt remonstrance you would kill Wang Jiao and paint the war drum with his blood? That crosses the line!"

sentences.zh: 」敦乃止。

translations.literal: Dun thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun relented.

sentences.zh: 敦既誅害忠賢，而稱疾不朝，將還武昌。

translations.literal: After Dun had slain and harmed loyal worthies, yet claimed illness and did not attend court, he was about to return to Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: After murdering loyalists Wang Dun feigned illness and prepared to withdraw to Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 鯤喻敦曰：「公大存社稷，建不世之勳，然天下之心實有未達。

translations.literal: Kun instructed Dun, "Your Grace greatly preserved the altars and established a merit not of a single generation, yet the mind of All-under-Heaven in truth has not yet reached understanding.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Kun urged him to face the emperor and heal the realm's mistrust.

sentences.zh: 若能朝天子，使君臣釋然，萬物之心於是乃服。

translations.literal: If you can attend the Son of Heaven and cause ruler and minister to release their doubts, then the mind of the myriad things will thereupon submit.
translations.idiomatic: A royal audience would calm court and country.

sentences.zh: 杖眾望以順群情，盡沖退以奉主上，如斯則勳侔一匡，名垂千載矣。

translations.literal: Relying on the multitude's hope to follow crowd feeling, exhausting humble yielding to serve the sovereign—if so then merit matches the one rectification and name hangs for a thousand ages."
translations.idiomatic: Humility before the throne would crown your deed for ages."

sentences.zh: 」敦曰：「君能保無變乎？

translations.literal: Dun said, "Can you guarantee no change?"
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun asked, "Can you guarantee no treachery?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「鯤近日入覲，主上側席，遲得見公，宮省穆然，必無虞矣。

translations.literal: He answered, "Kun recently entered audience; the sovereign sat sideways on the mat, delaying until he could see Your Grace; palace and ministries were solemn—surely there is no worry.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Kun swore the emperor waited eagerly and the palace was calm.

sentences.zh: 公若入朝，鯤請侍從。

translations.literal: If Your Grace enters court, Kun requests to attend as follower."
translations.idiomatic: "Let me escort you in."

sentences.zh: 」敦勃然曰：「正復殺君等數百人，亦復何損于時！

translations.literal: Dun suddenly roused said, "Even if I again kill you gentlemen several hundred people, again what harm would it do to the times!"
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun roared that killing hundreds would not matter.

sentences.zh: 」竟不朝而去。

translations.literal: In the end he did not attend court and departed.
translations.idiomatic: He marched away without an audience.

sentences.zh: 是時朝望被害，皆為其憂。

translations.literal: At the time court hope who were harmed all worried for him.
translations.idiomatic: Friends feared for Xie Kun's life.

sentences.zh: 而鯤推理安常，時進正言。

translations.literal: Yet Kun reasoned principle and settled the constant, from time to time advancing straight words.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Xie Kun stayed calm and spoke plain truth.

sentences.zh: 敦既不能用，內亦不悅。

translations.literal: Dun could not use him and inwardly was also not pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun ignored his counsel and nursed resentment.

sentences.zh: 軍還，使之郡，涖政清肅，百姓愛之。

translations.literal: When the army returned he sent him to his commandery; his governance was clear and stern, the hundred surnames loved him.
translations.idiomatic: Sent to his province, he ruled cleanly and the people loved him.

sentences.zh: 尋卒官，時年四十三。

translations.literal: Soon he died in office, aged forty-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office at forty-three.

sentences.zh: 敦死後，追贈太常，諡曰康。

translations.literal: After Dun's death he was posthumously awarded minister of rites, posthumous name Kang.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Dun fell he was canonized minister of rites as "Kang."

sentences.zh: 子尚嗣，別有傳。

translations.literal: His son Shang inherited; he has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xie Shang has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 胡毋輔之

translations.literal: Hu Wu Fuzhi (section heading).
translations.idiomatic: Biography of Hu Wu Fuzhi.

sentences.zh: 胡毋輔之，字彥國，泰山奉高人也。

translations.literal: Hu Wu Fuzhi, courtesy name Yanguo, was a native of Fenggao in Mount Tai.
translations.idiomatic: Huwu Fuzhi, courtesy Yanguo, came from Fenggao in Taishan.

sentences.zh: 高祖班，漢執金吾。

translations.literal: His high ancestor Ban was Han Bearer of the Golden Mace.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestor Huwu Ban was Bearer of the Golden Mace under Han.

sentences.zh: 父原，練習兵馬，山濤稱其才堪邊任，舉為太尉長史，終河南令。

translations.literal: His father Yuan was practiced in military affairs; Shan Tao said his talent matched border duty; he was raised to chief clerk to the grand commandant and ended as magistrate of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: His father Huwu Yuan was a soldier-scholar praised by Shan Tao and ended as magistrate of Henan.

sentences.zh: 輔之少擅高名，有知人之鑒。

translations.literal: Fuzhi in youth monopolized a lofty name and had the mirror of knowing men.
translations.idiomatic: Youth brought him fame and a knack for reading character.

sentences.zh: 性嗜酒，任縱不拘小節。

translations.literal: By nature he loved wine, trusted himself to abandon restraint and did not bind himself to small points.
translations.idiomatic: He drank freely and scorned petty scruples.

sentences.zh: 與王澄、王敦、庾敳俱為太尉王衍所昵，號曰四友。

translations.literal: Together with Wang Cheng, Wang Dun, and Yu Kai he was favored by Grand Commandant Wang Yan, called the Four Friends.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan favored him with Wang Cheng, Wang Dun, and Yu Kai as the "Four Friends."

sentences.zh: 澄嘗與人書曰：「彥國吐佳言如鋸木屑，霏霏不絕，誠為後進領袖也。」

translations.literal: Cheng once wrote someone saying, "Yanguo spits fine words like sawdust from sawing wood, drifting unceasingly—he is truly leader of the younger set."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Cheng wrote that Fuzhi showered wit like sawdust—leader of the rising generation.

sentences.zh: 辟別駕、太尉掾，並不就。

translations.literal: He was summoned as aide-de-camp and clerk to the grand commandant; both he did not take.
translations.idiomatic: He declined aide posts to the grand commandant.

sentences.zh: 以家貧，求試守繁昌令，始節酒自厲，甚有能名。

translations.literal: Because his household was poor he begged probationary governor of Fanchang; then he moderated wine and disciplined himself, having very able reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Poor, he took acting magistrate of Fanchang, sobered up, and earned a capable name.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted Gentleman of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Gentleman of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 豫討齊王冏，賜爵陰平男。

translations.literal: He participated in attacking Prince of Qi Sima Jiong and was enfeoffed as baron of Yinping.
translations.idiomatic: He helped crush Sima Jiong and won the Yinping barony.

sentences.zh: 累轉司徒左長史。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly transferred to chief clerk of the left in the ministry of education.
translations.idiomatic: He became chief clerk of the left in the ministry of education.

sentences.zh: 復求外出，為建武將軍、樂安太守。

translations.literal: Again he begged to go out and served as General Who Establishes Might and governor of Le'an.
translations.idiomatic: He then sought field duty as General Who Establishes Might and governor of Le'an.

sentences.zh: 與郡人光逸晝夜酣飲，不視郡事。

translations.literal: With a townsman Guang Yi he drank deep day and night and did not look at commandery affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He drank day and night with Guang Yi and ignored the yamen.

sentences.zh: 成都王穎為太弟，召為中庶子，遂與謝鯤、王澄、阮修、王尼、畢卓俱為放達。

translations.literal: Prince of Chengdu Sima Ying as heir apparent summoned him as retainer to the heir; thereupon together with Xie Kun, Wang Cheng, Ruan Xiu, Wang Ni, and Bi Zhuo he was reckoned unrestrained.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Ying was heir apparent, Fuzhi joined the carousing set with Xie Kun and others.

sentences.zh: 嘗過河南門下飲，河南騶王子博箕坐其傍，輔之叱使取火。

translations.literal: Once passing the gate of Henan he drank; Henan outrider Wang Zibo sat legs sprawled beside him; Fuzhi shouted ordering him to fetch fire.
translations.idiomatic: Drinking at the Henan commandery gate, he ordered a courier Wang Zibo to fetch a light.

sentences.zh: 子博曰：「我卒也，惟不乏吾事則已，安復為人使！

translations.literal: Zibo said, "I am lowly; only that I do not lack my own business is enough—how again would I be made to serve others!"
translations.idiomatic: The man snapped that he served no one.

sentences.zh: 」輔之因就與語，歎曰：「吾不及也！

translations.literal: Fuzhi thereupon drew near and spoke with him, sighed, "I do not match him!"
translations.idiomatic: Huwu Fuzhi talked with him and cried, "I am not his peer!"

sentences.zh: 」薦之河南尹樂廣，廣召見，甚悅之，擢為功曹。
