translations.literal: He recommended him to Henan governor Yue Guang; Guang summoned and saw him, greatly pleased with him, and promoted him to merit assessor.
translations.idiomatic: He recommended Wang Zibo to Yue Guang, who made him merit assessor.

sentences.zh: 其甄拔人物若此。

translations.literal: His discerning promotion of men was like this.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his eye for talent.

sentences.zh: 胡毋謙之

translations.literal: Hu Wu Qianzhi (section heading).
translations.idiomatic: His son Hu Wu Qianzhi.

sentences.zh: 謙之字子光。

translations.literal: Qianzhi, courtesy name Ziguang.
translations.idiomatic: Huwu Qianzhi, courtesy Ziguang,

sentences.zh: 才學不及父，而傲縱過之。

translations.literal: Talent and learning did not match his father, yet arrogance and abandon surpassed him.
translations.idiomatic: fell short of his father's learning but outdid him in swagger.

sentences.zh: 至酣醉，常呼其父字，輔之亦不以介意，談者以為狂。

translations.literal: When extremely drunk he constantly called his father's courtesy name; Fuzhi also did not take it as matter for mind; discussers thought him mad.
translations.idiomatic: Drunk, he called his father "Yanguo" to his face; Fuzhi only laughed—others called him mad.

sentences.zh: 輔之正酣飲，謙之規而厲聲曰：「彥國年老，不得為爾！

translations.literal: While Fuzhi was just drinking deep, Qianzhi peered in and in stern voice said, "Yanguo is old; you must not do this!
translations.idiomatic: Once, as Fuzhi drank, his son barked, "Old Yanguo, stop this—"

sentences.zh: 將令我尻背東壁。

translations.literal: You will make me buttocks and back to the eastern wall."
translations.idiomatic: you will leave me arse to the east wall!"

sentences.zh: 」輔之歡笑，呼入與共飲。

translations.literal: Fuzhi laughed in delight, called him in to drink together.
translations.idiomatic: Fuzhi laughed him inside to share the jar.

sentences.zh: 其所為如此。

translations.literal: His conduct was of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: Such were his ways.

sentences.zh: 年未三十卒。

translations.literal: Before thirty he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died before thirty.

sentences.zh: 畢卓字茂世，新蔡鮦陽人也。

translations.literal: Bi Zhuo, courtesy name Maoshi, was a native of Tongyang in Xincai.
translations.idiomatic: Bi Zhuo, courtesy Maoshi, came from Tongyang in Xincai.

sentences.zh: 父諶，中書郎。

translations.literal: His father Chen was gentleman of the palace secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His father Bi Chen was a palace secretary.

sentences.zh: 卓少希放達，為胡毋輔之所知。

translations.literal: Zhuo in youth hoped for abandon and was known to Hu Wu Fuzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Youthful Bi Zhuo yearned for freedom and won Huwu Fuzhi's notice.

sentences.zh: 太興末，為吏部郎，常飲酒廢職。

translations.literal: In the last years of Taixing he was director in the Ministry of Appointments, constantly drinking wine and ruining office duties.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Taixing he was personnel director who drank away his duties.

sentences.zh: 比舍郎釀熟，卓因醉夜至其甕間盜飲之，為掌酒者所縛，明旦視之，乃畢吏部也，遽釋其縛。

translations.literal: The neighboring gentleman's brew ripened; Zhuo because drunk at night went to his jars between and stole drink; he was bound by the wine steward; next morning looking at him, it was Bi of the Ministry of Appointments; they hastily released his bonds.
translations.idiomatic: A neighbor's wine matured; Bi Zhuo, drunk, raided the vats at night and was tied up by the cellar master—come dawn they found the thief was the personnel minister himself and cut him loose.

sentences.zh: 卓遂引主人宴于甕側，致醉而去。

translations.literal: Zhuo thereupon led the host to feast beside the jars, reached drunkenness and departed.
translations.idiomatic: He dragged the owner into a binge beside the casks, then staggered off.

sentences.zh: 卓嘗謂人曰：「得酒滿數百斛船，四時甘味置兩頭，右手持酒杯，左手持蟹螯，拍浮酒船中，便足了一生矣。

translations.literal: Zhuo once told someone, "If I could get wine filling several hundred hu in a boat, the four seasons' sweet flavors placed at both ends, right hand holding wine cup, left hand holding crab claws, splashing floating in the wine boat, that would be enough to finish one life."
translations.idiomatic: He said life would be complete with a boatload of wine, delicacies fore and aft, a cup in one hand and crab claws in the other, splashing midstream.

sentences.zh: 」及過江，為溫嶠平南長史，卒官。

translations.literal: When he crossed the river he became chief clerk to Wen Jiao who pacifies the south; he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: South of the Yangzi he served Wen Jiao as chief clerk and died in harness.

sentences.zh: 王尼，字孝孫，城陽人也，或云河內人。

translations.literal: Wang Ni, courtesy name Xiaosun, was a man of Chengyang; some say a man of Henei.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ni, courtesy Xiaosun, was said to hail from Chengyang or Henei.

sentences.zh: 本兵家子，寓居洛陽，卓犖不羈。

translations.literal: Originally a soldier's son, he lodged in Luoyang, outstanding and unrestrained.
translations.idiomatic: Son of a soldier family in Luoyang, he was bold and unbending.

sentences.zh: 初為護軍府軍士，胡毋輔之與琅邪王澄、北地傅暢、中山劉輿、潁川荀邃、河東裴遐迭屬河南功曹甄述及洛陽令曹攄請解之。

translations.literal: At first he was a soldier in the guards general's office; Hu Wu Fuzhi together with Wang Cheng of Langye, Fu Chang of Beidi, Liu Yu of Zhongshan, Xun Sui of Yingchuan, Pei Xia of Hedong in turn entrusted Henan merit assessor Zhen Shu and Luoyang magistrate Cao Shu requesting to release him.
translations.idiomatic: Huwu Fuzhi, Wang Cheng, Fu Chang, Liu Yu, Xun Sui, and Pei Xia petitioned the Henan clerks to free him from military service.

sentences.zh: 攄等以制旨所及，不敢。

translations.literal: Shu and others because it touched imperial regulation did not dare.
translations.idiomatic: The magistrates dared not break the rules.

sentences.zh: 輔之等齎羊酒詣護軍門，門吏疏名呈護軍，護軍歎曰：「諸名士持羊酒來，將有以也。

translations.literal: Fuzhi and others brought sheep and wine to the guards general's gate; the gate clerk wrote names and presented them to the guards general; the guards general sighed, "The various famed scholars bring sheep and wine—they must have a reason."
translations.idiomatic: They arrived with mutton and wine; the gate captain reported up; the general muttered that such a deputation meant trouble.

sentences.zh: 」尼時以給府養馬，輔之等入，遂坐馬廄下，與尼炙羊飲酒，醉飽而去，竟不見護軍。

translations.literal: At the time Ni because supplying the office was tending horses; Fuzhi and others entered, then sat beneath the horse stable with Ni, roasted sheep and drank wine, drunk and full departed, in the end did not see the guards general.
translations.idiomatic: They bypassed the general, roasted mutton in Wang Ni's stable, drank their fill, and left.

sentences.zh: 護軍大驚，即與尼長假，因免為兵。

translations.literal: The guards general was greatly startled, at once gave Ni long leave, and thereby freed him from being a soldier.
translations.idiomatic: The general, stunned, gave Wang Ni long leave and struck him from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 東嬴公騰辟為車騎府舍人，不就。

translations.literal: Duke of Dongying Teng summoned him as retainer to the chariot-and-horse office; he did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Teng offered him a staff post; he refused.

sentences.zh: 時尚書何綏奢侈過度，尼謂人曰：「綏居亂世，矜豪乃爾，將死不久。

translations.literal: At the time Minister He Sui was extravagant beyond measure; Ni told someone, "Sui dwells in a chaotic age yet flaunts pride thus—he will not long before death."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ni said wastrel He Sui would not live long in troubled times.

sentences.zh: 」人曰：「伯蔚聞言，必相危害。

translations.literal: Someone said, "If Boyu hears your words he will surely harm you mutually."
translations.idiomatic: Friends warned He Sui would retaliate.

sentences.zh: 」尼曰：「伯蔚比聞我語，已死矣。

translations.literal: Ni said, "Boyu compared to hearing my words is already dead."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ni answered that He Sui was already a dead man walking.

sentences.zh: 」未幾，綏果為東海王越所殺。

translations.literal: Before long Sui indeed was killed by Prince of the East Sea Sima Yue.
translations.idiomatic: He Sui soon fell to Sima Yue's purge.

sentences.zh: 初入洛，尼詣越不拜。

translations.literal: When first entering Luo, Ni visited Yue and did not bow.
translations.idiomatic: Entering Luoyang he refused to bow to Sima Yue.

sentences.zh: 越問其故，尼曰：「公無宰相之能，是以不拜。

translations.literal: Yue asked the reason; Ni said, "Your Grace lacks the ability of a chancellor of state; therefore I do not bow."
translations.idiomatic: He said Sima Yue lacked the talent of a true chancellor.

sentences.zh: 」因數之，言甚切。

translations.literal: Thereupon he enumerated faults, his words very cutting.
translations.idiomatic: He listed the warlord's failings bluntly.

sentences.zh: 又云：「公負尼物。

translations.literal: Again he said, "Your Grace owes Ni goods."
translations.idiomatic: He added that Sima Yue owed him a debt.

sentences.zh: 」越大驚曰：「寧有是也？

translations.literal: Yue was greatly startled and said, "Could there be such a thing?"
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yue gaped—how could that be?

sentences.zh: 」尼曰：「昔楚人亡布，謂令尹盜之。

translations.literal: Ni said, "In old days a man of Chu lost cloth and said the chief intendant stole it.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ni cited the parable of the lost cloth blamed on the chief minister.

sentences.zh: 今尼屋舍資財，悉為公軍人所略，尼今饑凍，是亦明公之負也。

translations.literal: Now Ni's houses and goods were entirely plundered by Your Grace's soldiers; Ni now is cold and hungry—this too is what Your Grace owes.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yue's troops had stripped him bare—so the debt was real.

sentences.zh: 」越大笑，即賜絹五十匹。

translations.literal: Yue laughed greatly and at once bestowed fifty bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yue roared with laughter and handed him fifty bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 諸貴人聞，競往餉之。

translations.literal: The various nobles hearing of it vied to go supply him.
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang grandees showered him with gifts.

sentences.zh: 洛陽陷，避亂江夏。

translations.literal: When Luoyang fell he fled turmoil to Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: When Luoyang fell he fled to Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 時王登為荊州刺史，遇之甚厚。

translations.literal: At the time Wang Deng was inspector of Jingzhou and treated him very generously.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhou inspector Wang Deng treated him kindly.

sentences.zh: 尼早喪婦，止有一子。

translations.literal: Ni early lost his wife; he had only one son.
translations.idiomatic: Widowed early, he had one son.

sentences.zh: 無居宅，惟畜露車，有牛一頭，每行，輒使子禦之，暮則共宿車上。

translations.literal: He had no dwelling; only he kept an open cart and one ox; each time traveling he always had his son drive it; at evening they lodged together on the cart.
translations.idiomatic: Homeless, he lived in an ox-cart with his boy.

sentences.zh: 常歎曰：「滄海橫流，處處不安也。

translations.literal: He constantly sighed, "The deep sea flows crosswise; everywhere is not secure."
translations.idiomatic: He sighed that chaos left nowhere safe.

sentences.zh: 」俄而澄卒，荊土饑荒，尼不得食，乃殺牛壞車，煮肉啖之。

translations.literal: Soon Cheng died; the Jing region suffered famine; Ni could not obtain food, thereupon killed the ox and broke the cart, boiled the meat and ate it.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Deng died and famine struck, he slaughtered his ox and burned his cart for food.

sentences.zh: 既盡，父子俱餓死。

translations.literal: When it was exhausted, father and son both starved to death.
translations.idiomatic: When the food ran out, father and son starved.

sentences.zh: 羊曼，字祖延，太傅祜兄孫也。

translations.literal: Yang Man, courtesy name Zuyan, was a grandson-on-the-brother's-line of Grand Tutor Yang Hu.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Man, courtesy Zuyan, descended from Yang Hu's brother's line.

sentences.zh: 父暨，陽平太守。

translations.literal: His father Ji was governor of Yangping.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yang Ji governed Yangping.

sentences.zh: 曼少知名，本州禮命，太傅辟，皆不就。

translations.literal: Man in youth was renowned; the province's ritual summons and Grand Tutor summons he all did not take.
translations.idiomatic: Youth brought fame; he spurned provincial and court summons.

sentences.zh: 避難渡江，元帝以為鎮東參軍，轉丞相主簿，委以機密。

translations.literal: Fleeing disaster he crossed the river; Emperor Yuan appointed him adjutant to the general who guards the east, was transferred chief clerk to the chancellor, entrusting him with secret matters.
translations.idiomatic: East of the river he became Sima Rui's adjutant and confidential clerk.

sentences.zh: 曆黃門侍郎、尚書吏部郎、晉陵太守，以公事免。

translations.literal: He served as Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, director in the Ministry of Appointments, governor of Jinling, dismissed for a public matter.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to personnel director and Jinling governor until a public scandal dismissed him.

sentences.zh: 曼任達穨縱，好飲酒。

translations.literal: Man was broad-minded and abandoned restraint, fond of drinking wine.
translations.idiomatic: He drank freely and lived loose.

sentences.zh: 溫嶠、庾亮、阮放、桓彝同志友善，並為中興名士。

translations.literal: Wen Jiao, Yu Liang, Ruan Fang, Huan Yi were like-minded friends, together famed worthies of the restoration.
translations.idiomatic: He ran with Wen Jiao, Yu Liang, Ruan Fang, and Huan Yi—stars of the Eastern Jin revival.

sentences.zh: 時州裏稱陳留阮放為宏伯，高平郗鑒為方伯，泰山胡毋輔之為達伯，濟陰卞壺為裁伯，陳留蔡謨為朗伯，阮孚為誕伯，高平劉綏為委伯，而曼為濌伯，凡八人，號兗州八伯，蓋擬古之八雋也。

translations.literal: At the time the province styled Chenliu Ruan Fang Hongbo, Gaoping Xi Jian Fangbo, Mount Tai Hu Wu Fuzhi Dabo, Jiyin Bian Kun Caibo, Chenliu Cai Mo Langbo, Ruan Fu Danbo, Gaoping Liu Sui Weibo, while Man was Tubo—eight men in all, called the Eight Barons of Yanzhou, roughly modeled on the Eight Paragons of antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Man headed the "Eight Barons" clique aping the Han Eight Paragons—each man had a mock noble title.

sentences.zh: 王敦既與朝廷乖貳，羈錄朝士，曼為右長史。

translations.literal: After Wang Dun had become at odds with the court and detained court gentlemen, Man became his chief clerk of the right.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Dun held the capital, Yang Man became his chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 曼知敦不臣，終日酣醉，諷議而已。

translations.literal: Man knew Dun was not a loyal subject; all day he drank deep and only mildly remonstrated.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing Wang Dun's treason, he stayed drunk and offered only veiled advice.

sentences.zh: 敦以其士望，厚加禮遇，不委以事，故得不涉其難。

translations.literal: Dun because of his scholarly reputation treated him generously with courtesy, did not entrust him with affairs, therefore he was able not to be drawn into that disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun honored his name but gave him no real work, sparing him the purge.

sentences.zh: 敦敗，代阮孚為丹陽尹。

translations.literal: After Dun's defeat he replaced Ruan Fu as governor of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Dun fell he became governor of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 時朝士過江初拜官，相飾供饌。

translations.literal: At the time court gentlemen who had crossed the river on first appointment mutually supplied feasts.
translations.idiomatic: New southern appointees vied to host banquets.

sentences.zh: 曼拜丹陽，客來早者得佳設，日宴則漸罄，不復及精，隨客早晚而不問貴賤。

translations.literal: When Man took office as Danyang governor, guests who came early obtained fine provisions; toward evening banquet they gradually ran out, no longer reaching excellence; he followed guests early or late without asking noble or base.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Man's feasts started lavish for early guests and thinned by night—he never ranked guests by rank.

sentences.zh: 有羊固拜臨海太守，竟日皆美，雖晚至者猶獲盛饌。

translations.literal: There was Yang Gu appointed governor of Linhai; the whole day all was fine; although those who arrived late still obtained lavish fare.
translations.idiomatic: His kinsman Yang Gu fed everyone lavishly all day, even latecomers.

sentences.zh: 論者以固之豐腆，乃不如曼之真率。

translations.literal: Discussers because Gu's abundance was not as good as Man's genuine frankness.
translations.idiomatic: Critics said Yang Gu's opulence lacked Yang Man's honest ease.

sentences.zh: 蘇峻作亂，加前將軍，率文武守雲龍門。

translations.literal: When Su Jun rebelled he was given former general and led civil and military to guard Cloud Dragon Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Su Jun's revolt won him general's rank to hold Cloud Dragon Gate.

sentences.zh: 王師不振，或勸曼避峻。

translations.literal: Royal troops did not rally; some urged Man to avoid Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial forces faltered; friends urged retreat.

sentences.zh: 曼曰：「朝廷破敗，吾安所求生？

translations.literal: Man said, "The court is broken and defeated—where would I seek life?"
translations.idiomatic: Where could a loyalist flee for life?

sentences.zh: 」勒眾不動，為峻所害，年五十五。

translations.literal: He pressed his host not to move and was killed by Jun, aged fifty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He held his post and died to Su Jun at fifty-five.

sentences.zh: 峻平，追贈太常。

translations.literal: When Jun was pacified he was posthumously awarded minister of rites.
translations.idiomatic: After Su Jun fell he was canonized minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 子賁嗣，少知名，尚明帝女南郡悼公主，除秘書郎，早卒。

translations.literal: His son Ben inherited; in youth renowned, he married Emperor Ming's daughter Princess Dao of Nan commandery, was appointed gentleman of the palace secretariat, died early.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yang Ben married Mingdi's daughter and died young.

sentences.zh: 弟聃。

translations.literal: Younger brother Dan.
translations.idiomatic: His brother was Yang Dan.

sentences.zh: 聃字彭祖。

translations.literal: Dan, courtesy name Pengzu.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Dan, courtesy Pengzu.

sentences.zh: 少不經學，時論皆鄙其凡庸。

translations.literal: In youth he did not pursue classical learning; contemporary discussion all despised him as commonplace.
translations.idiomatic: He skipped scholarship and was mocked as dull.

sentences.zh: 先是，兗州有八伯之號，其後更有四伯。

translations.literal: Before this Yanzhou had the title of Eight Barons; afterward there were again Four Barons.
translations.idiomatic: After the Eight Barons came the "Four Barons" mockery.

sentences.zh: 大鴻臚陳留江泉以能食為谷伯，豫章太守史疇以大肥為笨伯，散騎郎高平張嶷以狡妄為猾伯，而聃以狼戾為瑣伯，蓋擬古之四凶。

translations.literal: Grand herald of Chenliu Jiang Quan because able to eat was called Grain Baron; governor of Yuzhang Shi Chou because very fat was called Stout Baron; gentleman of the palace Zhang Ni of Gaoping because crafty and false was called Sly Baron, while Dan because fierce and cruel was called Petty Baron—roughly modeled on the Four Fiends of antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Dan was dubbed "Petty Baron" beside three other jest titles, aping the Four Fiends.

sentences.zh: 聃初辟元帝丞相府，累遷廬陵太守。

translations.literal: Dan at first was summoned to Emperor Yuan's chancellor's office, repeatedly promoted governor of Luling.
translations.idiomatic: He entered Yuan's chancellery and rose to governor of Luling.

sentences.zh: 剛克粗暴，恃國戚，縱恣尤甚，睚眥之嫌輒加刑殺。

translations.literal: He was rigid, harsh, and violent, relying on imperial kinship, indulging license especially severely; a sidelong grudge he would punish with killing.
translations.idiomatic: Brutal and well-connected, he killed over slights.

sentences.zh: 疑郡人簡良等為賊，殺二百餘人，誅及嬰孩，所髡鎖復百餘。

translations.literal: Suspecting townsman Jian Liang and others of being bandits, he killed more than two hundred people, executions reaching infants; those shaved and chained again exceeded a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: He massacred over two hundred—including babies—on a bandit scare.

sentences.zh: 庾亮執之，歸於京都。

translations.literal: Yu Liang seized him and sent him to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Liang arrested him for the capital.

sentences.zh: 有司奏聃罪當死，以景獻皇后是其祖姑，應八議。

translations.literal: Responsible officials reported Dan's crime deserved death; because Empress Jingxian was his great-aunt by marriage, he should receive the eight deliberations.
translations.idiomatic: The law demanded death, but kinship to the empress triggered the eight deliberations.

sentences.zh: 成帝詔曰：「此事古今所無，何八議之有！

translations.literal: Emperor Cheng's edict said, "This affair is without parallel in ancient and modern—what eight deliberations could there be!"
translations.idiomatic: Chengdi called the case unprecedented—no eight deliberations.

sentences.zh: 猶未忍肆之市朝，其賜命獄所。

translations.literal: Still I cannot bear to expose him in market and court; grant him ordered suicide in prison.
translations.idiomatic: He spared public execution and ordered prison suicide.

sentences.zh: 」兄子賁尚公主，自表求解婚。

translations.literal: His nephew Ben had married a princess; he memorialized requesting dissolution of the marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Prince-in-law Yang Ben begged to divorce him.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「罪不相及，古今之令典也。

translations.literal: An edict said, "Guilt does not extend to others—this is the standing rule of ancient and modern.
translations.idiomatic: An edict cited the rule that guilt does not taint kin.

sentences.zh: 聃雖極法，于賁何有！

translations.literal: Although Dan suffers extreme law, what has it to do with Ben!
translations.idiomatic: Yang Dan's guilt should not stain Yang Ben.

sentences.zh: 其特不聽離婚。

translations.literal: Especially do not permit divorce.
translations.idiomatic: The throne refused the divorce.

sentences.zh: 」琅邪太妃山氏，聃之甥也，入殿叩頭請命。

translations.literal: Grand consort of Langye, Lady Shan, Dan's niece, entered the hall knocking head begging for his life.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Shan, Yang Dan's niece, fell to her knees to plead for his life.

sentences.zh: 王導又啟：「聃罪不容恕，宜極重法。

translations.literal: Wang Dao again submitted: "Dan's crime brooks no forgiveness—he should receive the heaviest law.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dao urged maximum punishment.

sentences.zh: 山太妃憂戚成疾，陛下罔極之恩，宜蒙生全之宥。

translations.literal: Grand Consort Shan worries sick with grief; Your Majesty's boundless grace ought to receive the indulgence that preserves life.
translations.idiomatic: Yet killing him might kill the grieving grand consort.

sentences.zh: 」於是詔下曰：「太妃惟此一舅，發言摧咽，乃至吐血，情慮深重。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict went down saying, "The Grand Consort has only this one maternal uncle; when she speaks her throat is torn and she even vomits blood—her feeling and thought are deep and heavy.
translations.idiomatic: A second edict cited Lady Shan's grief.

sentences.zh: 朕往丁荼毒，受太妃撫育之恩，同於慈親。

translations.literal: I formerly suffered bitter poison and received the Grand Consort's nurturing grace, the same as a loving parent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor recalled her nurture like a mother's.

sentences.zh: 若不堪難忍之痛，以致頓弊，朕亦何顏以寄。

translations.literal: If I could not bear the pain hard to endure, thereby causing collapse, what face would I have to rely on.
translations.idiomatic: He feared her death more than his own shame.

sentences.zh: 今便原聃生命，以慰太妃渭陽之思。

translations.literal: Now let us spare Dan's life to comfort the Grand Consort's Wei-yang longing.
translations.idiomatic: He spared Yang Dan to console Lady Shan.

sentences.zh: 」於是除名。

translations.literal: Thereupon his name was stricken.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Dan was stripped of office.

sentences.zh: 頃之，遇疾，恆見簡良等為祟，旬日而死。

translations.literal: Before long he fell ill, constantly seeing Jian Liang and others as haunting spirits; within ten days he died.
translations.idiomatic: Soon visions of his victims drove him mad and he died within days.

sentences.zh: 光逸，字孟祖，樂安人也。

translations.literal: Guang Yi, courtesy name Mengzu, was a man of Le'an.
translations.idiomatic: Guang Yi, courtesy Mengzu, came from Le'an.

sentences.zh: 初為博昌小吏，縣令使逸送客，冒寒舉體凍濕，還遇令不在，逸解衣炙之，入令被中臥。

translations.literal: At first he was a petty clerk in Bochang; the county magistrate ordered Yi to escort a guest; braving cold his whole body was frozen wet; returning he met the magistrate absent; Yi removed his clothes to roast them, entered the magistrate's quilt and lay down.
translations.idiomatic: A frozen courier, he warmed himself in his boss's bed.

sentences.zh: 令還，大怒，將加嚴罰。

translations.literal: When the magistrate returned he was greatly angry and was about to apply harsh punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The magistrate returned furious.

sentences.zh: 逸曰：「家貧衣單，沾濕無可代。

translations.literal: Yi said, "My household is poor and clothes are thin; soaked wet there is nothing to replace.
translations.idiomatic: Guang Yi pleaded poverty—his clothes were soaked.

sentences.zh: 若不暫溫，勢必凍死，奈何惜一被而殺一人乎！

translations.literal: If I did not warm briefly, the situation would surely freeze to death—how could one cherish one quilt and kill a person!
translations.idiomatic: Without warmth he would freeze—better than dying for modesty.

sentences.zh: 君子仁愛，必不爾也，故寢而不疑。

translations.literal: A gentleman's benevolent love surely would not be thus; therefore I slept without doubt.
translations.idiomatic: A humane magistrate would not punish that sleep.

sentences.zh: 」令奇而釋之。

translations.literal: The magistrate marveled and released him.
translations.idiomatic: The magistrate spared him.

sentences.zh: 後為門亭長，迎新令至京師。

translations.literal: Later he became head of the gate pavilion, welcoming the new magistrate to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He later greeted a new magistrate bound for the capital.

sentences.zh: 胡毋輔之與荀邃共詣令家，望見逸，謂邃曰：「彼似奇才。

translations.literal: Hu Wu Fuzhi together with Xun Sui together visited the magistrate's house; looking from afar they saw Yi; they said to Sui, "That one seems a marvelous talent."
translations.idiomatic: Huwu Fuzhi and Xun Sui spotted him as a genius in the street.

sentences.zh: 」便呼上車，與談良久，果俊器。

translations.literal: Thereupon they called him into the carriage and spoke with him a long time; indeed he was a splendid vessel.
translations.idiomatic: They hauled him into a carriage for a long talk and confirmed his brilliance.

sentences.zh: 令怪客不入，吏白與光逸語。

translations.literal: The magistrate wondered the guests did not enter; clerks reported they were conversing with Guang Yi.
translations.idiomatic: The magistrate fumed that his guests dallied with a clerk.

sentences.zh: 令大怒，除逸名，斥遣之。

translations.literal: The magistrate was greatly angry, struck Yi's name from the rolls, and expelled him.
translations.idiomatic: He struck Guang Yi from the roster.

sentences.zh: 後舉孝廉，為州從事，棄官投輔之。

translations.literal: Later recommended filial and incorrupt, he became clerk to the province, cast aside office and threw himself to Fuzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended as filial, he quit to join Huwu Fuzhi.

sentences.zh: 輔之時為太傅越從事中郎，薦逸於越，越以門寒而不召。

translations.literal: At the time Fuzhi was gentleman of the staff to Grand Tutor Yue and recommended Yi to Yue; Yue because the gate was cold did not summon him.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yue snubbed him as low-born despite Fuzhi's memo.

sentences.zh: 越後因閑宴，責輔之無所舉薦。

translations.literal: Later Yue because of a leisure feast blamed Fuzhi for recommending nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Later at a banquet Sima Yue scolded Fuzhi for poor recommendations.

sentences.zh: 輔之曰：「前舉光逸，公以非世家不召，非不舉也。

translations.literal: Fuzhi said, "Earlier I recommended Guang Yi; Your Grace because he was not a hereditary house did not summon him—it is not that I did not recommend."
translations.idiomatic: Fuzhi answered that Guang Yi had been recommended but blackballed for pedigree.

sentences.zh: 」越即辟焉。

translations.literal: Yue at once summoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yue summoned him on the spot.

sentences.zh: 書到郡縣，皆以為誤，審知是逸，乃備禮遣之。

translations.literal: When the writ reached command and county all thought it mistaken; verifying that it was Yi, they then prepared full ritual and sent him off.
translations.idiomatic: Local clerks thought the summons a mistake until they saw his name.

sentences.zh: 尋以世難，避亂渡江，復依輔之。

translations.literal: Soon because of troubles of the age he fled turmoil crossing the river, again relying on Fuzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He fled south with the court and again joined Fuzhi.

sentences.zh: 初至，屬輔之與謝鯤、阮放、畢卓、羊曼、桓彝、阮孚散發裸袒，閉室酣飲已累日。

translations.literal: When first arriving, it happened Fuzhi together with Xie Kun, Ruan Fang, Bi Zhuo, Yang Man, Huan Yi, Ruan Fu had loosened hair and bared bodies, closed the chamber and drunk deep already many days.
translations.idiomatic: He arrived while Huwu Fuzhi and friends had been naked, hair down, drinking behind locked doors for days.

sentences.zh: 逸將排戶入，守者不聽，逸便於戶外脫衣露頭于狗竇中窺之而大叫。

translations.literal: Yi was about to push the door to enter; the guard would not permit; Yi then outside the door removed clothes and exposed his head in the dog hole to peek and greatly shouted.
translations.idiomatic: Blocked at the door, Guang Yi stripped and shoved his head through the dog flap, shouting.

sentences.zh: 輔之驚曰：「他人決不能爾，必我孟祖也。

translations.literal: Fuzhi startled said, "Another person by no means could do thus—it must be my Mengzu."
translations.idiomatic: Huwu Fuzhi shouted, "No one else would dare—that is my Guang Yi!"

sentences.zh: 」遽呼入，遂與飲，不舍晝夜。

translations.literal: Thereupon called him to enter, thereupon drank with him, not letting up day or night.
translations.idiomatic: They hauled him in and drank without pause for days.

sentences.zh: 時人謂之八達。

translations.literal: People of the time called them the Eight Unimpeded.
translations.idiomatic: Onlookers dubbed them the Eight Free Spirits.

sentences.zh: 元帝以逸補軍諮祭酒。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan used Yi to fill out army consultant libationer.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan appointed Guang Yi army adviser with libationer's stipend.

sentences.zh: 中興建，為給事中，卒官。

translations.literal: At the restoration's founding he became palace counselor and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: When the Eastern Jin court stood, he became palace counselor and died in harness.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：夫學非常道，則物靡不通；

translations.literal: The historiographer says: As for learning without the constant Way, then things are without nothing not penetrated;
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: without a fixed Way, inquiry reaches everywhere;

sentences.zh: 理有忘言，則在情斯遣。

translations.literal: When principle has forgetting words, then in disposition that is what is cast aside.
translations.idiomatic: when truth outruns speech, passion falls away.

sentences.zh: 其進也，撫俗同塵，不居名利；

translations.literal: Their advance: stroking the vulgar sharing dust, not dwelling in name and profit;
translations.idiomatic: In office they mingled with dust and shunned fame;

sentences.zh: 其退也，餐和履順，以保天真。

translations.literal: their retreat: eating harmony treading compliance, thereby to preserve heaven's genuineness.
translations.idiomatic: in withdrawal they harmonized with nature and kept Heaven's core.

sentences.zh: 若乃一其本原，體無為之用，分其華葉，開寓言之道，是以伯陽垂范，鳴謙置式，欲崇諸己，先下於人，猶大樂無聲，而蹌鸞斯應者也。

translations.literal: If unifying their root source, embodying non-action's function, dividing their flowering foliage, opening fable's Way—thereupon Boyang left model, sounding modesty establishing pattern, wishing to elevate what is in oneself, first lowering to others—it is like supreme music without sound, yet the mincing phoenixes respond thereby.
translations.idiomatic: Laozi modeled silence, Zhuangzi spun fables—like soundless music that still draws the phoenix dance.

sentences.zh: 莊生放達其旨，而馳辯無窮；

translations.literal: Master Zhuang abandoned restraint in his gist, yet galloped in disputation without end;
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzi preached release yet argued without end;

sentences.zh: 棄彼榮華，則俯輕爵位，懷其道術，則顧蔑王公；

translations.literal: cast aside that glory-blossom, then bowing lightly to noble rank; embracing their path and art, then glancing to despise kings and dukes;
translations.idiomatic: they scorned tinsel rank yet scorned kings who wore it;

sentences.zh: 舐痔兼車，鳴鳶吞腐。

translations.literal: licking piles sharing carriages, crying kites swallowing rot.
translations.idiomatic: they mocked lickers of sores and crows at carrion—Zhuangzi's bitter jests.

sentences.zh: 以茲自口，於焉玩物，殊異虛舟，有同攘臂。

translations.literal: Using these from their mouths, thereupon playing with things—utterly different from empty boat, yet the same as rolling up sleeves.
translations.idiomatic: Their talk toyed with scandal the way Zhuangzi's empty boat excuses rage—yet it stirred the age like rolled sleeves.

sentences.zh: 嵇、阮竹林之會，劉、畢芳樽之友，馳騁莊門，排登李室。

translations.literal: Ji and Ruan's Bamboo Grove meetings, Liu and Bi's fragrant goblet friends—galloped Zhuang's gate, pushed Li's chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Kang's circle drank Zhuang's wine yet camped in Laozi's quiet.

sentences.zh: 若夫儀天布憲，百官從軌，經禮之外，棄而不存。

translations.literal: If there is spanning heaven spreading norm, hundred officials following track—beyond canonical ritual they cast aside and do not preserve.
translations.idiomatic: Where heaven's pattern needs officials in harness, they cast ritual aside.

sentences.zh: 是以帝堯縱許由於埃盍之表，光武舍子陵於潺湲之瀨，松蘿低舉，用以優賢，岩水澄華，茲焉賜隱；

translations.literal: Therefore Emperor Yao released Xu You beyond the dust's surface, Guangwu set aside Ziling on the chattering shallows—pine and vine low-lifted, used thereby to honor worthies; cliff waters clear-splendid, hereby granting hiding;
translations.idiomatic: So Yao exalted Xu You beyond the dust, Guangwu left Yan Ziling on the stream—landscape itself became the stipend of reclusion;

sentences.zh: 臣行厥志，主有嘉名。

translations.literal: ministers acted their intent, sovereigns gained fine names.
translations.idiomatic: ministers kept their vows, rulers kept repute.

sentences.zh: 至於嵇康遺巨源之書，阮氏創先生之傳，軍諮散發，吏部盜樽，豈以世疾名流，茲焉自垢？

translations.literal: As for Ji Kang's letter left to Giant Source, the Ruan clan's creation of "Account of the Great Man," army consultant loosening hair, ministry stealing the goblet—was it that the age hated famous currents, thereupon here soiled themselves?
translations.idiomatic: From Ji's break with Shan Tao to Ruan's "Great Man," from naked advisers to stolen wine—were they fouling themselves because the age despised fame?

sentences.zh: 臨鍛灶而不回，登廣武而長歎，則嵇琴絕響，阮氣徒存。

translations.literal: Facing the forge and not turning back, climbing Guangwu and long sighing—then Ji's zither cut off its sound, Ruan's pneuma vainly survived.
translations.idiomatic: At the forge and Guangwu Pass they sealed Ji Kang's silent zither and Ruan Ji's lonely breath.

sentences.zh: 通其旁徑，必凋風俗；

translations.literal: Open their side paths—surely they will wither custom;
translations.idiomatic: Their shortcuts wither public morals;

sentences.zh: 召以效官，居然屍素。

translations.literal: summon them to serve in office—suddenly they are mere rice-bags.
translations.idiomatic: call them to office and they become empty sacks.

sentences.zh: 軌躅之外，或有可觀者焉。

translations.literal: Beyond tracks and footprints, perhaps there is still something worth observing.
translations.idiomatic: Yet beyond the ruts they still reward the gaze.

sentences.zh: 咸能符契情靈，各敦終始，愴神交於晚笛，或相思而動駕。

translations.literal: All were able to tally and match with spiritual disposition, each thick in end and start, moving spirit-communion in evening flute, some longing in thought and stirring carriage.
translations.idiomatic: They answered spirit with spirit—flute notes at dusk, carriages racing for a last word.

sentences.zh: 史臣是以拾其遺事，附於篇雲。

translations.literal: The historiographer therefore gathers their leftover affairs and appends them at chapter's end.
translations.idiomatic: So this chapter gathers their scattered tales.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：老篇爰植，孔教提衡。

translations.literal: The eulogy says: Laozi's chapters planted, Confucian teaching holds the scales.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium sings: Laozi planted the seed, Confucius weighed the scales;

sentences.zh: 各存其趣，道貴無名。

translations.literal: Each keeps its interest; the Way esteems having no name.
translations.idiomatic: each path keeps its charm, yet the nameless Way is highest;

sentences.zh: 相彼非禮，遵乎達生。

translations.literal: Look at those who flouted ritual—they followed the fulfilled life.
translations.idiomatic: Those who flouted ritual were chasing the art of the fulfilled life.

sentences.zh: 秋水揚波，春雲斂映。

translations.literal: Autumn waters raise waves, spring clouds gather gleams.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn floods lift long waves; spring clouds soften the sunlight.

sentences.zh: 旨酒厥德，憑虛其性。

translations.literal: Fine wine its virtue, leaning on void its nature.
translations.idiomatic: Fine wine was their virtue; emptiness was their nature.

sentences.zh: 不玩斯風，誰虧王政？

translations.literal: Who unless playing this wind, who thereupon injures kingship?
translations.idiomatic: Who could condemn their temper without faulting the throne?
